Title: Understanding Your Invoice
Summary: Every Nimbus Workspace invoice lists your plan name, billing period, seat count, any add-ons, applicable tax, and the total charged to your payment method on file. Paid plans are billed in advance — monthly plans on the same calendar day each month, annual plans on your subscription anniversary. Line items separate the base subscription cost from add-ons like extra storage or premium integrations, and from any prorated charges caused by mid-cycle seat changes. View or download any invoice from Billing Settings > Invoice History; invoices are also emailed to your billing contact the day they're generated.

Title: How Proration Works When You Change Plans
Summary: When you upgrade or downgrade between Team, Business, and Enterprise mid-cycle, Nimbus Workspace calculates a prorated charge or credit based on the days remaining in your current billing period. Upgrades take effect immediately and the prorated difference is charged right away. Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing cycle, so you keep current-plan features until then — no partial-period credit is issued for a downgrade. Adding or removing seats mid-cycle follows the same per-seat, per-remaining-day proration logic.

Title: Accepted Payment Methods
Summary: Nimbus Workspace accepts Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover for all self-serve Team and Business plans, charged automatically each billing cycle. Enterprise customers on an annual contract can pay by ACH bank transfer or against a Purchase Order invoice, arranged through your account executive. PayPal, wire transfer for self-serve plans, and cryptocurrency are not supported. Only one payment method can be on file per workspace at a time; adding a new card replaces the previous one for future charges.

Title: Updating Your Credit Card on File
Summary:
To update the card charged for your subscription:

  1. Go to Billing Settings from your workspace admin console.
  2. Select Payment Method, then Edit.
  3. Enter the new card number, expiration date, and billing zip code.
  4. Click Save — the new card is validated with a $0 authorization check.
  5. Your next scheduled charge, and any future renewals, will use the new card automatically.

Past invoices are not affected by a payment method change.

Title: Why Was I Charged Twice This Month?
Summary: A duplicate-looking charge is almost always one of three things: a prorated upgrade charge appearing alongside your regular renewal, a failed payment retry that succeeded on a second attempt (the first attempt should show as declined, not charged), or an add-on purchase (extra storage, a premium integration) billed separately from the base subscription. Check Billing Settings > Invoice History — each charge maps to a specific invoice with a line-item breakdown. If two invoices genuinely charge the same line item for the same period, contact Billing Support with both invoice numbers for a refund.

Title: Plan Comparison & Switching
Summary:
Nimbus Workspace offers four plans: Free (up to 5 users, 2GB storage), Team ($12/user/month, 50GB pooled storage, automations), Business ($24/user/month, 250GB pooled storage, SSO, advanced reporting), and Enterprise (custom pricing, unlimited storage, SCIM provisioning, dedicated support). To switch plans:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Plan.
  2. Select Compare Plans to see the full feature matrix.
  3. Choose the target plan and click Change Plan.
  4. Review the prorated charge or credit shown before confirming.
  5. Confirm — the change applies immediately for upgrades, or at next renewal for downgrades.

Title: Downgrading Your Subscription
Summary:
Downgrades to a lower plan tier take effect at the start of your next billing cycle, not immediately — you keep full access to your current plan's features until then. To downgrade:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Plan > Change Plan.
  2. Select the lower-tier plan.
  3. Review the feature-loss warning (e.g., SSO, advanced reporting are Business/Enterprise-only).
  4. Confirm the scheduled downgrade.
  5. You'll receive a confirmation email with the effective date; you can cancel the scheduled downgrade any time before then.

Title: How Seat-Based Billing Works
Summary: Team and Business plans bill per active user seat. A seat is consumed by any user with Owner, Admin, or Member access; Guest users (view/comment-only on shared projects) do not consume a seat. Your invoice reflects the highest seat count reached during the billing period for monthly plans, or the seat count at contract signing (with a true-up at renewal) for annual and Enterprise plans. Deactivating a user frees their seat for reassignment immediately, but does not generate a mid-cycle refund for that seat.

Title: Adding or Removing Seats Mid-Cycle
Summary: Adding a seat mid-cycle bills a prorated amount for the remaining days in the current period, charged on your next invoice. Removing a seat (by deactivating a user) frees the seat for reassignment immediately but does not issue a prorated credit — the seat count for billing purposes is based on peak usage during the period on monthly plans. Annual and Enterprise contracts true-up seat counts at renewal rather than mid-term, so removing a seat mid-contract reduces cost only at the next renewal.

Title: Annual vs. Monthly Billing Cycles
Summary: Monthly billing charges your card every 30 days at standard per-seat rates. Annual billing charges once per year, up front, at a discounted rate (typically a 15–20% savings versus twelve monthly payments), and is required for Enterprise contracts. You can switch from monthly to annual at any time from Billing Settings — the switch takes effect at your next renewal date and locks in the annual rate. Switching from annual to monthly is only available at the end of your current annual term.

Title: Requesting a Refund
Summary: Annual plan subscribers can request a prorated refund for unused months within 30 days of the renewal charge by contacting Billing Support with their invoice number. Monthly plan charges are non-refundable once processed, but you can cancel at any time to prevent future charges — your access continues through the end of the paid period. Add-on purchases (extra storage, premium integrations) follow the same 30-day annual / non-refundable monthly policy as the base subscription. Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method within 5–7 business days.

Title: Understanding Your Free Trial Period
Summary: New Business and Enterprise plan signups include a 14-day free trial with full feature access and no credit card required to start. A trial banner shows the number of days remaining in your workspace. You can invite teammates, connect integrations, and import data during the trial exactly as on a paid plan — nothing is limited except the trial's duration. Adding a payment method at any point during the trial converts it to a paid subscription immediately and stops the trial countdown.

Title: What Happens When Your Trial Ends
Summary: If no payment method is added before your 14-day trial ends, your workspace automatically converts to the Free plan rather than being deleted. Any data or configuration created beyond Free plan limits (extra seats, storage over 2GB, premium integrations) becomes read-only until you upgrade again — nothing is deleted. You'll receive reminder emails at 7 days, 3 days, and on the final day of your trial with a direct link to add a payment method and continue uninterrupted on your trial plan.

Title: Applying a Coupon or Promo Code
Summary:
To apply a promotional code to your subscription:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Plan.
  2. Click Have a promo code?
  3. Enter the code exactly as provided (codes are case-sensitive).
  4. Click Apply — the discount and its expiration, if any, will display before you confirm.
  5. Confirm your plan change or renewal to lock in the discounted rate.

Only one promo code can be active per workspace at a time; applying a new code replaces the previous one.

Title: Tax Exemption Certificates
Summary: Nonprofit, government, and educational organizations with valid tax-exemption status can submit a certificate to be excluded from sales tax on future invoices. Email your certificate to billing@nimbusworkspace.com along with your workspace ID. Processing takes 3–5 business days, and exemption applies to invoices generated after approval — it is not retroactive to past invoices. Certificates must be renewed with Nimbus Workspace whenever your organization's exemption status is renewed by the issuing authority, typically annually.

Title: Multi-Currency Invoicing
Summary: Self-serve Team and Business plans are billed in USD regardless of your organization's location. Enterprise customers on an annual contract can request invoicing in EUR, GBP, AUD, or CAD through their account executive; the exchange rate is locked at contract signing and re-evaluated at each annual renewal. Multi-currency invoicing is not available for monthly self-serve plans. All invoices, regardless of currency, itemize the same line items — base subscription, add-ons, tax, and any proration.

Title: Enterprise Purchase Order (PO) Billing
Summary: Enterprise customers can pay against a Purchase Order instead of a credit card. To set this up, your account executive issues a formal quote; once you return a signed order form and PO number, Nimbus Workspace generates a NET-30 invoice referencing that PO number. PO-based invoices are sent directly to your accounts payable contact rather than charged automatically. Renewal invoices are generated 45 days before the contract end date to allow time for a new PO to be issued if needed.

Title: Downloading Past Invoices as PDF
Summary:
To download a copy of any past invoice:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Invoice History.
  2. Find the invoice by date or invoice number using the search field.
  3. Click the row to expand the line-item detail.
  4. Click Download PDF in the top right of the expanded view.
  5. The PDF includes your company's billing address and tax ID if one is on file, suitable for expense reporting or accounting records.

Title: Failed Payment & Dunning Emails
Summary: If a scheduled charge fails (expired card, insufficient funds, bank decline), Nimbus Workspace retries automatically after 1, 3, and 7 days, sending a dunning email reminder at each attempt with a link to update your payment method. Your workspace remains fully functional during the retry window. If all three retries fail, the workspace is downgraded to a restricted state (read-only for anything beyond Free plan limits) until a valid payment method is added and the outstanding balance is charged.

Title: Updating Your Billing Contact
Summary: The billing contact receives all invoices, payment-failure notices, and renewal reminders — they don't need to be a workspace Admin. To update it, go to Billing Settings > Billing Contact, enter the new name and email address, and click Save. You can also add a secondary billing contact (Business and Enterprise plans only) so notices go to two recipients, useful when finance and IT need visibility into the same billing events.

Title: Understanding Add-On Charges
Summary: Add-ons are billed separately from your base subscription and appear as distinct line items on your invoice. Current add-ons include extra pooled storage blocks (100GB increments), the premium integrations bundle (advanced Jira and GitHub sync), and priority support (guaranteed 4-hour response SLA). Add-ons purchased mid-cycle are prorated like a seat addition; removing an add-on takes effect at your next renewal, consistent with the downgrade policy for the base plan.

Title: Understanding Enterprise Custom Pricing
Summary: Enterprise pricing is quoted per organization based on seat count, contract length, data residency requirements, and any add-ons like SCIM provisioning or a dedicated customer success manager. There is no public list price for Enterprise — request a quote through the in-app Contact Sales link or your account executive. Enterprise quotes typically include volume-based per-seat discounts that improve at higher seat tiers and multi-year commitment discounts for 2- and 3-year terms.

Title: Cancelling Your Subscription
Summary:
To cancel your Nimbus Workspace subscription:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Plan.
  2. Click Cancel Subscription at the bottom of the page.
  3. Select a cancellation reason from the short survey (optional but helps us improve).
  4. Confirm cancellation — you'll see the exact date access changes.
  5. Your workspace remains fully functional through the end of the current paid period, then automatically converts to the Free plan; no further charges occur.

Title: Reactivating a Cancelled Account
Summary:
If you cancelled and your workspace converted to the Free plan, all your data is preserved and reactivating is immediate:

  1. Log in to your workspace as before — cancellation does not lock you out.
  2. Go to Billing Settings > Plan.
  3. Select the plan you'd like to reactivate on.
  4. Enter or confirm your payment method.
  5. Confirm — full plan features are restored immediately, with no re-import needed.

Workspace data is retained for 90 days after cancellation before any purge, well beyond typical reactivation windows.

Title: Volume Discounts for Large Teams
Summary: Organizations purchasing 100 or more seats on an annual Business or Enterprise plan qualify for tiered volume discounts, ranging from 5% at 100 seats to 20% at 1,000+ seats. Volume pricing is automatically calculated on annual Business plan quotes generated through Contact Sales, and is built into every Enterprise quote by default. Volume discounts apply to the base subscription only, not to add-ons, and require an annual (not monthly) commitment.

Title: Non-Profit and Education Discounts
Summary: Registered nonprofits and accredited educational institutions qualify for a 30% discount off standard Team and Business plan pricing. To apply, submit proof of nonprofit or education status (a 501(c)(3) determination letter, or a .edu domain verification) through Contact Sales. Approved discounts apply at the next renewal and must be re-verified annually. The discount can be combined with annual billing savings but not with other promotional codes.

Title: Contract Renewal Notices
Summary: Annual and Enterprise contracts trigger an automatic renewal notice 60 days before the contract end date, sent to your billing contact and account owner, followed by a second reminder at 30 days. Contracts renew automatically at the then-current rate unless cancelled before the renewal date or a new negotiated rate is in place. Enterprise customers working with an account executive typically begin renewal quote discussions at the 90-day mark to allow time for procurement review.

Title: Billing Cycle Start Date Changes
Summary: Your billing cycle start date is fixed to the day you first subscribed and generally cannot be changed without cancelling and resubscribing, which would forfeit any pro-rated time remaining. Enterprise customers can request a one-time billing-date alignment (for example, to match a fiscal year start) through their account executive; this is handled as a one-time prorated adjustment invoice rather than a plan change, and is available only at contract renewal or upon initial signing.

Title: VAT and GST on International Invoices
Summary: Nimbus Workspace charges VAT, GST, or other applicable sales tax based on your workspace's registered billing country, in compliance with local tax law. If your organization has a valid VAT or GST registration number, add it under Billing Settings > Tax Information — invoices generated afterward will apply the reverse-charge mechanism where applicable, showing 0% tax with your registration number referenced. Adding a tax ID does not affect previously issued invoices.

Title: Understanding Usage-Based Overage Charges
Summary: Storage and API usage on Team and Business plans are pooled allowances, not hard caps — exceeding your plan's included storage or API rate limit doesn't block usage but triggers an overage charge on your next invoice (billed per additional 10GB block for storage; API overages are throttled per FR2.4-style rate limiting rather than billed). Enterprise plans typically negotiate unlimited storage with a fair-use policy instead of overage billing. You can monitor current usage against your plan limits from the Admin Console usage dashboard.

Title: Splitting an Invoice Across Departments
Summary:
Business and Enterprise plans support cost-center tagging so a single consolidated invoice can be split for internal chargeback:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Cost Centers.
  2. Create a cost center for each department (e.g., Engineering, Marketing).
  3. Assign each user to a cost center from the Team Directory.
  4. Generate a Cost Center Breakdown report from Billing Settings > Reports.
  5. Export the breakdown as CSV for your finance team — Nimbus Workspace still issues one invoice; the breakdown is informational, not a split billing arrangement.

Title: Setting a Spending Limit for Add-Ons
Summary:
Admins can cap how much any user is allowed to spend on self-serve add-ons without additional approval:

  1. Go to Billing Settings > Spending Controls.
  2. Toggle on Require approval for add-on purchases.
  3. Set a monthly spending limit per workspace.
  4. Choose which roles can approve requests that exceed the limit (Owner and Admin by default).
  5. Save — any add-on purchase attempt beyond the limit now generates an approval request instead of charging immediately.

Title: What's Included in the Enterprise Plan
Summary: Enterprise includes everything in Business (SSO, advanced reporting, 250GB+ storage) plus SCIM user provisioning, unlimited storage with a fair-use policy, a dedicated customer success manager, a custom Data Processing Agreement, priority support with a 4-hour SLA, single-tenant API keys, and support for a custom data residency region. Enterprise is the only plan tier that supports Purchase Order billing and multi-year contract terms.

Title: Free Plan Limitations
Summary: The Free plan supports up to 5 users, 2GB of pooled file storage, unlimited projects and tasks, and access to the mobile apps, but does not include automations, SSO, advanced reporting, guest access, or API access beyond basic read-only endpoints. Free plan projects can be upgraded to a paid plan at any time with no data migration required — all existing tasks, comments, and files carry over immediately once you upgrade.

Title: How to Read Your Billing History
Summary: Billing Settings > Invoice History lists every invoice in reverse chronological order, showing the date, invoice number, amount, and payment status (Paid, Pending, Failed). Clicking a row expands the full line-item breakdown, including any proration, add-ons, tax, and discounts applied. A Payment Status filter lets you quickly find failed or pending charges, and a date-range filter supports pulling a full year's history for expense reconciliation.

Title: Payment Declined — What To Do
Summary: A declined payment usually means an expired card, insufficient funds, or your bank's fraud filter blocking an unfamiliar merchant charge. First, confirm your card details and expiration date under Billing Settings > Payment Method. If details are correct, contact your card issuer to authorize charges from "Nimbus Workspace Inc." Nimbus Workspace automatically retries a declined charge at 1, 3, and 7 days; you can also trigger a manual retry immediately after updating your payment method rather than waiting for the next scheduled attempt.

Title: Switching From Monthly to Annual Billing
Summary: Switching to annual billing locks in a discounted rate and consolidates twelve payments into one. From Billing Settings > Plan, select Switch to Annual — the change takes effect at your next monthly renewal date, at which point you're charged the full annual amount and your renewal date shifts to a yearly cadence. There's no mid-month proration for this switch; it simply takes effect at the next scheduled renewal.

Title: Requesting a Custom Enterprise Contract
Summary:
Organizations needing custom contract terms (a Master Service Agreement, non-standard payment terms, a specific liability cap, or a custom Data Processing Agreement) should work with an account executive rather than self-serve billing:

  1. Submit a request via the in-app Contact Sales link, selecting Custom Contract.
  2. An account executive reaches out within 1 business day to scope requirements.
  3. Legal and Security review any requested contract or DPA changes (typically 5–10 business days).
  4. A redlined agreement is circulated for signature via the org's chosen e-signature tool.
  5. Once signed, billing converts to the negotiated terms at the next renewal or immediately, per the contract's effective date.

Title: Understanding Seat True-Up at Renewal
Summary: Annual and Enterprise contracts are priced for a committed seat count at signing. If your actual active-user count exceeds that commitment during the year, a true-up invoice is generated at renewal for the additional seats, prorated for the portion of the year they were active. True-up never happens mid-contract — only at renewal — so adding users during the year doesn't trigger an immediate extra charge, only a reconciliation at the next annual invoice.

Title: Billing Support Contact Options
Summary: Billing questions can be routed through in-app chat (select the Billing topic for fastest routing), email at billing@nimbusworkspace.com, or, for Enterprise customers, directly through your dedicated customer success manager. Standard billing support responds within 1 business day; Enterprise's 4-hour SLA also covers billing inquiries. Have your invoice number or workspace ID ready — it lets support pull up your account immediately without additional verification steps.

Title: Gift or Sponsored Subscriptions
Summary: A third party (a parent company, an accelerator program, or a partner organization) can sponsor a workspace's subscription by being added as an alternate billing contact with payment authorization. Contact Billing Support with written consent from both the workspace owner and the sponsoring party to set this up. Sponsored subscriptions still show standard invoices to the workspace owner for transparency, but charges route to the sponsor's payment method instead.

Title: Currency Conversion and Exchange Rate Timing
Summary: For Enterprise contracts invoiced in a non-USD currency, the exchange rate is locked at the time of contract signing or renewal, not recalculated per invoice — so your per-seat local-currency price stays stable for the full contract term even if exchange rates fluctuate. The rate is re-evaluated only at the next annual renewal, using the prevailing rate at that time, and any change is disclosed in the renewal quote before you commit.

Title: Consolidated Billing for Multiple Workspaces
Summary: Organizations running more than one Nimbus Workspace (for example, separate workspaces per subsidiary) can request consolidated billing through Enterprise sales, which combines all workspaces onto a single invoice and payment method while keeping each workspace's data, users, and admin permissions fully separate. Consolidated billing is configured by Nimbus Workspace's billing operations team and cannot currently be self-served — request it via Contact Sales, referencing all workspace IDs to include.

Title: End-of-Life Plan Migration (Legacy Plans)
Summary: Customers still on a discontinued legacy plan tier (from before the current Free/Team/Business/Enterprise structure) will receive a migration notice at least 90 days before the legacy plan is retired, along with a recommended equivalent current plan and any pricing grandfathering available. No action is required before the notice period ends — if you take no action, your workspace migrates automatically to the recommended plan at the stated date, preserving all existing data and configuration.

Title: Resetting Your Password
Summary:
If you've forgotten your password:

  1. Go to the Nimbus Workspace login page and click Forgot Password.
  2. Enter the email address associated with your account.
  3. Check your inbox for a password reset email (arrives within a few minutes).
  4. Click the reset link, which is valid for 60 minutes.
  5. Enter a new password meeting the minimum complexity requirements and confirm.

If you don't receive the email, check your spam folder or confirm you're using the correct sign-in email — SSO-enabled accounts don't use a Nimbus Workspace password at all.

Title: Setting Up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
Summary:
To enable 2FA on your account:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Security.
  2. Toggle on Two-Factor Authentication.
  3. Choose an authentication method: an authenticator app (TOTP) or SMS text message.
  4. If using an authenticator app, scan the displayed QR code and enter the 6-digit code to confirm.
  5. Save your backup codes somewhere safe — they're the only way back in if you lose access to your authentication method.

Title: Adding a Teammate to Your Workspace
Summary:
To invite a new teammate:

  1. Go to Team Directory from your workspace admin console.
  2. Click Invite Member.
  3. Enter their email address and select a role (Admin, Member, or Guest).
  4. Optionally assign them to specific projects during invite.
  5. Click Send Invite — they'll receive an email with a link to set up their account.

Invited users consume a seat as soon as they accept, not at the moment of invitation.

Title: Removing a User from Your Workspace
Summary: To remove a teammate, go to Team Directory, find the user, and select Deactivate from the row's action menu. Deactivating immediately revokes their access and frees their seat for reassignment, but preserves their historical activity (comments, task completions) attributed to their name for audit purposes. Deactivated users can be reactivated later without losing their history. To permanently delete a user's data entirely, use Delete User instead, which is irreversible and typically used only for compliance-driven removals.

Title: Understanding User Roles and Permissions
Summary: Nimbus Workspace has four built-in roles: Owner (full control, including billing and workspace deletion — exactly one per workspace), Admin (manage users, projects, and settings, no billing access by default), Member (create and edit tasks/projects they're added to), and Guest (view and comment only on projects explicitly shared with them, no seat consumed). Business and Enterprise plans additionally support custom roles built from granular permission sets for teams needing finer-grained access control.

Title: Creating a Custom Permission Set
Summary:
Business and Enterprise plans can define custom roles beyond the four built-in ones:

  1. Go to Team Directory > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Click Create Custom Role.
  3. Name the role and select individual permissions (create projects, delete tasks, manage integrations, view billing, etc.).
  4. Save the role.
  5. Assign it to users from their profile in the Team Directory.

Custom roles can be edited later; existing users assigned to a role automatically inherit any permission changes.

Title: Managing Guest Access
Summary: Guests are external collaborators given view/comment access to specific shared projects without consuming a paid seat. To invite a guest, open the project, click Share, enter their email, and select Guest as the access level. Guests can comment on tasks and upload files but cannot create new tasks, change project settings, or see other projects in your workspace. Admins can review and revoke all active guest access workspace-wide from Team Directory > Guest Access.

Title: Changing Your Account Email Address
Summary: To change the email address used to sign in, go to Account Settings > Profile, click Change next to your email, and enter the new address. A verification link is sent to the new email; your sign-in email doesn't change until you click that link, which prevents accidental lockouts from a typo. If your account uses SSO, your email is managed by your identity provider and must be changed there rather than in Nimbus Workspace directly.

Title: Updating Your Display Name and Avatar
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Profile to update your display name, profile photo, and job title as shown to teammates across tasks, comments, and mentions. Changes take effect immediately across the workspace, including in past comments (the name shown always reflects your current profile, not a historical snapshot). Profile photos support JPG and PNG up to 5MB; if none is uploaded, initials are shown instead on a colored avatar.

Title: Merging Duplicate User Accounts
Summary:
If a teammate accidentally created two accounts (for example, signing up with both a personal and work email), Admins can merge them:

  1. Go to Team Directory and identify the duplicate accounts.
  2. Select both accounts and choose Merge Accounts from the bulk action menu.
  3. Choose which account to keep as the primary.
  4. Confirm — all tasks, comments, and project memberships from the secondary account transfer to the primary.
  5. The secondary account is deactivated automatically once the merge completes.

This action cannot be undone, so confirm the correct primary account before proceeding.

Title: Transferring Workspace Ownership
Summary:
Every workspace has exactly one Owner with full billing and deletion authority. To transfer ownership:

  1. Go to Team Directory > Workspace Settings.
  2. Select Transfer Ownership.
  3. Choose an existing Admin as the new Owner (the recipient must already have an Admin role).
  4. Confirm — the recipient receives an email they must accept within 7 days.
  5. Once accepted, the previous Owner is automatically reassigned the Admin role.

Title: Deactivating vs. Deleting a User
Summary: Deactivating a user immediately revokes login access and frees their seat, while preserving their name on historical comments, task assignments, and audit logs — this is the recommended default for offboarding. Deleting a user permanently removes their profile information and reassigns their identity in historical records to "Former User," which is irreversible. Use deletion only when required for a specific compliance or data-minimization request, since it removes attribution from your workspace's history.

Title: Bulk Inviting Users via CSV
Summary:
To invite many users at once instead of one at a time:

  1. Go to Team Directory > Invite Member > Bulk Invite.
  2. Download the CSV template (columns: Email, Role, Project Assignment).
  3. Fill in one row per user and save the file.
  4. Upload the completed CSV.
  5. Review the preview of parsed rows, then click Send Invites — up to 500 rows can be processed in a single upload.

Title: Managing User Offboarding
Summary:
When someone leaves your organization, offboard them promptly to protect data and reclaim their seat:

  1. Go to Team Directory and locate the departing user.
  2. Reassign any tasks they own to a teammate using the Reassign Tasks action.
  3. Transfer ownership of any projects where they're listed as Project Owner.
  4. Select Deactivate from their row's action menu.
  5. For bulk departures (a layoff or team restructuring), use Bulk Deprovision Users to offboard multiple people in one action — removals affecting more than 25 users require an additional confirmation step.

Title: Setting a Default Role for New Members
Summary: Admins can set which role new invitees receive by default, so inviters don't need to select one manually each time. Go to Team Directory > Workspace Settings > Default Role and choose Member, Admin, or a custom role (Business/Enterprise). This default applies only to future invitations; it does not change the role of anyone already in the workspace. Individual invites can still override the default at the time of sending.

Title: Understanding Workspace Admin Privileges
Summary: Admins can manage users (invite, deactivate, change roles), create and configure projects workspace-wide, manage integrations, and view usage reports, but cannot access billing settings or delete the workspace itself — those remain Owner-only by default. Business and Enterprise plans can grant billing visibility to specific Admins individually via a custom permission set without making them the Owner.

Title: Recovering a Locked-Out Account
Summary: If you're locked out after too many failed login attempts, wait 15 minutes for the automatic lockout to clear, or use the Forgot Password flow to reset your password immediately, which also clears the lockout. If you've also lost access to your 2FA method, use one of your saved backup codes; if those are unavailable too, a workspace Admin can initiate an account recovery from Team Directory > Security > Reset 2FA, which requires identity verification with Nimbus Workspace Support.

Title: Session Timeout Settings
Summary: By default, web sessions time out after 24 hours of inactivity, requiring re-authentication. Business and Enterprise Admins can customize this under Workspace Settings > Security > Session Timeout, choosing any value between 1 and 24 hours, or enabling a shorter timeout specifically for sessions on unrecognized devices. Mobile app sessions persist longer by default (30 days) to avoid repeated logins on trusted personal devices, but can also be tightened by policy on Enterprise plans.

Title: Managing Multiple Workspaces Under One Login
Summary: A single Nimbus Workspace account (one email address) can belong to multiple workspaces — for example, a consultant working across several client organizations. Each workspace maintains entirely separate users, projects, and billing; your role can differ per workspace (Admin in one, Guest in another). There's no limit to how many workspaces one account can belong to, and being added to a new workspace never affects your existing memberships.

Title: Switching Between Workspaces
Summary: If your account belongs to more than one workspace, click your avatar in the top-left corner and select Switch Workspace from the dropdown to see the full list. Selecting a different workspace reloads the app in that workspace's context — your notifications, tasks, and settings are entirely separate per workspace. The mobile app supports the same switcher from the account menu, and remembers your last-used workspace on next launch.

Title: Setting Up Single Sign-On (SSO)
Summary:
Business and Enterprise plans support SAML 2.0 SSO with providers like Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Security > Single Sign-On.
  2. Select your identity provider or choose Generic SAML 2.0.
  3. Copy the Nimbus Workspace ACS URL and Entity ID into your identity provider's app configuration.
  4. Upload your identity provider's signing certificate and metadata into Nimbus Workspace.
  5. Enable Enforce SSO once you've tested a successful login, so all users are required to authenticate through your identity provider going forward.

Title: Configuring SCIM User Provisioning
Summary:
Enterprise plans support SCIM 2.0 for automated user provisioning and deprovisioning from your identity provider:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Security > SCIM Provisioning.
  2. Generate a SCIM API token (shown once — store it securely).
  3. Enter the Nimbus Workspace SCIM base URL and token into your identity provider's provisioning app.
  4. Map identity provider groups to Nimbus Workspace roles.
  5. Enable automatic deprovisioning so a user removed from your identity provider is deactivated in Nimbus Workspace within 15 minutes.

Title: Setting a Password Policy for Your Organization
Summary: Business and Enterprise Admins can enforce a minimum password policy for all non-SSO users under Workspace Settings > Security > Password Policy, including minimum length (8–20 characters), required character types (uppercase, number, symbol), and a maximum password age forcing periodic resets (30, 60, or 90 days, or never). Policy changes apply to the next password set by each user; existing passwords aren't invalidated retroactively unless you also enable Force Reset on Next Login.

Title: Understanding Login Notifications
Summary: Nimbus Workspace sends an email notification whenever your account is signed into from a new device or an unrecognized location, including the approximate location, device type, and time. This is separate from 2FA and cannot be disabled for security reasons, though Enterprise Admins can route these notifications to a shared security inbox in addition to the individual user. If you receive a notification for a login you don't recognize, change your password immediately and review Active Sessions.

Title: Restricting Login by IP Address
Summary: Enterprise plans support IP allowlisting to restrict workspace login to specific network ranges — typically a corporate VPN or office IP block. Configure this under Workspace Settings > Security > IP Allowlist by adding CIDR ranges. Once enabled, login attempts from outside the allowlist are blocked before password entry, with an explanatory message. Test the allowlist with a non-Admin account before fully enforcing it, since a misconfigured range can lock out your entire team, including Admins.

Title: Managing Pending Invitations
Summary: Go to Team Directory > Pending Invitations to see everyone who's been invited but hasn't yet accepted, along with the date sent and days remaining before expiration (invitations expire after 14 days). From this list you can resend an invitation, edit the assigned role before it's accepted, or revoke it entirely. Revoking an invitation immediately invalidates the invite link; the invited person will see an expired-invitation message if they try to use it afterward.

Title: Resending an Expired Invitation
Summary: Invitations expire 14 days after being sent if not accepted. To resend one, go to Team Directory > Pending Invitations, find the expired entry (marked with an Expired badge), and click Resend. This generates a fresh invite link with a new 14-day expiration; the original expired link will no longer work. You do not need to re-enter the invitee's email or role — those carry over from the original invitation automatically.

Title: Changing a User's Role
Summary: To change a teammate's role, go to Team Directory, find the user, and select their current role badge to open a dropdown of available roles. Role changes take effect immediately — a Member promoted to Admin gains new permissions on their very next page load, no re-login required. Downgrading a user's role can immediately remove their access to project settings or integrations they previously configured, so review their current responsibilities before downgrading.

Title: Viewing Active Sessions
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Security > Active Sessions to see every device and browser currently signed into your account, including the last-active time, approximate location, and device type. This is useful for confirming no one else is using your account. Each session can be individually revoked, or you can use Sign Out of All Devices to end every session at once, including your current one, requiring you to log back in.

Title: Signing Out of All Devices
Summary: If you suspect unauthorized access, go to Account Settings > Security > Active Sessions and click Sign Out of All Devices. This immediately invalidates every active session, including mobile app sessions and any browser tabs, requiring a fresh login everywhere. It's recommended to also change your password and review recent activity in the audit log immediately after doing this, in case the unauthorized session made any changes.

Title: Account Recovery Without Access to Email
Summary: If you've lost access to both your password and your recovery email, self-service reset isn't possible, since the reset link is the primary verification mechanism. Have a workspace Admin submit an account recovery request through Support on your behalf, providing identity verification (proof of employment or organizational affiliation) as required. Support will work with the Admin to verify your identity and either update your email on file or assist with a supervised password reset.

Title: Setting Up a Delegated Admin
Summary:
Owners can grant a trusted teammate Admin-level access without making them a full Admin across every setting, using a delegated admin scope:

  1. Go to Team Directory > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Select Add Delegated Admin.
  3. Choose the specific areas they can manage (user management only, integrations only, or a custom combination).
  4. Assign the scope to the chosen user.
  5. They'll see only the delegated sections in Workspace Settings — everything else remains hidden from their view.

Title: Understanding Seats vs. Guests
Summary: A seat is consumed by any Owner, Admin, or Member — these count toward your plan's billed user total. A Guest, by contrast, is an external collaborator with view/comment access to specific shared projects only, and does not consume a seat or count toward billing regardless of how many guests you invite. This distinction lets you collaborate with clients or contractors on specific projects without increasing your subscription cost.

Title: Renaming Your Workspace
Summary: Go to Workspace Settings > General > Workspace Name to rename your workspace. The new name updates immediately across the app, in emails sent to your team, and in the browser tab title. Renaming does not change your workspace's unique URL/subdomain; that requires a separate request through Support since it affects bookmarked links, SSO configuration, and any integrations pointing at the old subdomain.

Title: Setting Workspace-Level Default Time Zone
Summary: Go to Workspace Settings > General > Default Time Zone to set the time zone new users are assigned automatically, used for due dates, calendar sync, and scheduled automations until an individual changes their own profile time zone. Existing users' individually-set time zones are not affected by changing the workspace default; this setting only applies going forward to new members who haven't yet set a personal preference.

Title: Managing Notification Preferences
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Notifications to control which events trigger an email, an in-app notification, or a mobile push — task assignments, @mentions, due-date reminders, comment replies, and project status changes can each be configured independently. A Do Not Disturb schedule can also be set to pause non-urgent notifications outside working hours; @mentions can be exempted from Do Not Disturb individually if you still want to be reachable for direct call-outs.

Title: Linking a Google or Microsoft Account for Login
Summary:
Instead of a Nimbus Workspace password, you can sign in using an existing Google or Microsoft account:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Security > Linked Accounts.
  2. Select Link next to Google or Microsoft.
  3. Complete the provider's standard OAuth consent screen.
  4. Confirm the link — you can now sign in using either your password or the linked account.
  5. Unlinking is available from the same screen, provided you've set a Nimbus Workspace password as a fallback first.

Title: Understanding the Team Directory
Summary: Team Directory is the central admin view of every user in your workspace, showing their role, status (active, deactivated, pending invite), last login, and project memberships. Admins can filter by role or status, bulk-select users for actions like role changes or deactivation, and export the full directory to CSV for HR or audit purposes. It's also where custom roles, guest access, and pending invitations are managed from a single place.

Title: Setting Up Departments or Groups
Summary:
Business and Enterprise plans support organizing users into Departments or Groups for easier bulk management and reporting:

  1. Go to Team Directory > Departments.
  2. Click Create Department and name it (e.g., Engineering, Sales).
  3. Add existing users to the department individually or via bulk CSV upload.
  4. Optionally assign a department lead who can manage membership.
  5. Use departments as a filter in reports, cost-center billing, and bulk actions like project assignment.

Title: Exporting a List of Active Users
Summary: Go to Team Directory, apply any filters you want (role, status, department), and click Export CSV in the top right. The export includes name, email, role, status, last login date, and department, useful for HR audits, license reconciliation, or security reviews. Exports reflect a point-in-time snapshot; scheduled recurring exports (daily or weekly, delivered by email) are available on Business and Enterprise plans under Reports > Scheduled Exports.

Title: Understanding Inactive User Cleanup Policy
Summary: Users who haven't logged in for 180 consecutive days are flagged as Inactive in the Team Directory (with a visible badge) but are not automatically deactivated or removed — this is informational only, to help Admins identify stale seats worth reclaiming. Enterprise plans can opt into an automated policy that deactivates (not deletes) users past a configurable inactivity threshold, freeing their seat automatically, with a notification sent to Admins before each automated deactivation.

Title: Custom Roles vs. Standard Roles
Summary: Standard roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Guest) come with a fixed, non-editable set of permissions and are available on every plan. Custom roles (Business and Enterprise only) let you combine individual permissions — such as "can manage integrations" or "can view billing" — into a role tailored to your team's structure, without granting full Admin access. A user can only hold one role at a time, whether standard or custom.

Title: Managing Biometric Login on Mobile
Summary: The Nimbus Workspace mobile app supports Face ID and fingerprint unlock as a convenience layer on top of your existing login session — it does not replace your password or 2FA, it simply re-authenticates a device that's already signed in without retyping credentials each time. Enable it under the mobile app's Settings > Security > Biometric Unlock. If biometric authentication fails repeatedly, the app falls back to requiring your password.

Title: Closing Your Nimbus Workspace Account
Summary:
Closing your entire workspace (not just cancelling a subscription) permanently deletes all projects, tasks, files, and user accounts and cannot be undone. Only the Owner can initiate this:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > General > Close Workspace.
  2. Read the data-loss warning carefully — this is distinct from cancelling a paid plan, which retains data for 90 days.
  3. Type the workspace name to confirm intent.
  4. Confirm closure.
  5. Data is queued for permanent deletion within 30 days, consistent with our standard data retention policy for closed accounts.

Title: Creating Your First Workspace
Summary:
To set up your first Nimbus Workspace:

  1. Sign up at nimbusworkspace.com with your email address.
  2. Verify your email via the link sent to your inbox.
  3. Name your workspace (this becomes your workspace URL, e.g., yourcompany.nimbusworkspace.com).
  4. Choose a starting template or begin from a blank workspace.
  5. Invite your first teammates — you can always add more later from Team Directory.

Title: Creating Projects from Templates
Summary:
To start a new project from a template instead of blank:

  1. Click New Project from any workspace view.
  2. Select Browse Templates.
  3. Choose a category (Marketing, Engineering, Product Launch, Events, etc.) or search by keyword.
  4. Preview the template's included task lists, custom fields, and views.
  5. Click Use This Template — a new project is created pre-populated with the template's structure, ready to customize.

Title: Understanding Workspaces vs. Projects vs. Boards
Summary: A Workspace is your organization's entire account — all users, projects, and billing live under one workspace. A Project is a defined body of work with its own tasks, timeline, and team (e.g., "Q3 Website Redesign"). A Board is simply one way of viewing a project's tasks (Kanban-style columns); the same project's tasks can also be viewed as a List, Calendar, or Gantt chart — the underlying tasks are identical across all views, only the presentation changes.

Title: Setting Up a Kanban Board
Summary:
Every project defaults to a List view, but you can add a Board view:

  1. Open the project and click Add View.
  2. Select Board.
  3. Define your columns (commonly To Do, In Progress, Review, Done) — these map to the task's Status field.
  4. Drag existing tasks into the appropriate column, or create new tasks directly on the board.
  5. Reorder columns by dragging their headers; changes to the board don't affect the List or Gantt views of the same tasks.

Title: Switching Between List, Board, and Gantt Views
Summary: Every project can display its tasks in multiple views simultaneously — List, Board (Kanban), Calendar, and Gantt — accessible from the view tabs at the top of the project. Switching views doesn't change or duplicate your data; it's the same underlying set of tasks rendered differently. Any filter or sort you apply in one view is view-specific and doesn't carry over automatically to the others unless saved as a Saved View.

Title: Creating and Assigning Tasks
Summary: Click + New Task from any project view, enter a task name, and press Enter to create it instantly — additional details (assignee, due date, description, attachments) can be added by clicking into the task afterward. To assign it, click the assignee field and select a teammate from the project's member list; assigning a task automatically adds that person to the project if they weren't already a member, and triggers an assignment notification.

Title: Setting Task Dependencies
Summary:
To make one task wait on another:

  1. Open the task that should be blocked.
  2. Click Add Dependency.
  3. Select Blocked By and choose the prerequisite task.
  4. Save — the dependent task's due date will show a warning if it's scheduled before the prerequisite's due date.
  5. On the Gantt view, dependencies are shown as connecting lines between tasks, and shifting a prerequisite's date will prompt you to shift dependent tasks accordingly.

Title: Creating Subtasks
Summary: To break a task into smaller steps, open the parent task and click Add Subtask, then enter a name — subtasks appear as a checklist within the parent task and can each have their own assignee and due date. Completing all subtasks does not automatically complete the parent task; the parent must still be marked done explicitly, since a parent task can represent more than just the sum of its subtasks (e.g., a final review step).

Title: Setting Up Recurring Tasks
Summary:
To make a task repeat automatically:

  1. Open the task and click the due date field.
  2. Select Make Recurring.
  3. Choose a frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, or a custom interval).
  4. Choose whether the next occurrence is created when the current one is marked done, or on a fixed schedule regardless of completion.
  5. Save — a new instance of the task generates automatically according to your chosen rule, keeping the same assignee, description, and subtasks as a copy.

Title: Using Milestones to Track Progress
Summary: Milestones mark significant checkpoints in a project's timeline without being an actionable task themselves — for example, "Beta Launch" or "Contract Signed." Add one from the Gantt view by clicking Add Milestone and setting its date; milestones appear as a diamond marker distinct from regular task bars. Milestones can have dependencies just like tasks, so you can require several tasks to complete before a milestone is considered reached.

Title: Customizing Task Fields
Summary: Beyond the default fields (assignee, due date, status, priority), you can show or hide fields per project view by clicking the Fields icon and toggling visibility — this only affects what's displayed, not the underlying data, so hidden fields retain their values and can be re-shown anytime. Reordering fields in this menu also changes their column order in List view and their order on the task detail panel.

Title: Creating a Custom Field
Summary:
To add a field beyond the built-in ones:

  1. Go to the project's Settings > Fields.
  2. Click Add Custom Field.
  3. Choose a field type (Text, Number, Dropdown, Date, Checkbox, or Person).
  4. Name the field and, for Dropdown fields, define the selectable options.
  5. Save — the field is now available on every task in this project, and can optionally be applied workspace-wide from the same menu if you want it available in all projects.

Title: Setting Up Project Templates
Summary:
To turn an existing project into a reusable template:

  1. Open the project and go to Project Settings.
  2. Select Save as Template.
  3. Choose whether to include existing task assignees and due dates, or reset them for a clean template.
  4. Name the template and select a category for the template gallery.
  5. Save — the template is now available to your whole workspace under Browse Templates > My Workspace Templates.

Title: Duplicating a Project
Summary: To copy an existing project rather than starting from a template, open the project, click the (···) menu, and select Duplicate Project. Choose whether to carry over task assignees, due dates, comments, and attachments, or reset each independently — for example, keeping the task structure but clearing due dates for a project you're reusing on a new timeline. The duplicate is created as a new project and does not affect the original in any way.

Title: Archiving a Completed Project
Summary: Archiving removes a project from your active project list without deleting it — its tasks, comments, and files remain fully intact and searchable. Open the project, click the (···) menu, and select Archive Project. Archived projects can be restored at any time from Workspace Settings > Archived Projects, or filtered into view from the main project list using the Show Archived toggle.

Title: Restoring an Archived Project
Summary: To bring an archived project back into your active list, go to Workspace Settings > Archived Projects, find the project (searchable by name), and click Restore. The project reappears in the main project list exactly as it was when archived, including all tasks, comments, and views — nothing needs to be reconfigured. There's no limit to how long a project can remain archived before restoration.

Title: Deleting a Project
Summary: Deleting a project (distinct from archiving) permanently removes all its tasks, comments, and attachments after a 30-day recovery window. Only Admins and the Project Owner can delete a project, and a confirmation dialog requires typing the project name to proceed. During the 30-day window, a deleted project can be recovered from Workspace Settings > Trash; after 30 days, it's purged permanently and cannot be recovered by Support.

Title: Setting Project Start and Due Dates
Summary: Go to Project Settings > Timeline to set an overall project start and due date, shown at the top of the Gantt view and used in portfolio-level reporting to flag at-risk projects. Individual task due dates are independent of the project-level dates and are not automatically constrained by them — setting a project due date doesn't prevent a task from having a later date, though the Gantt view will visually flag tasks that extend past the project's end date.

Title: Understanding Workload View
Summary: Workload view shows each team member's assigned tasks across all their projects in a single timeline, color-coded by how many hours or tasks are scheduled per day relative to their configured capacity, helping spot over-allocation before it becomes a bottleneck. Access it from the workspace-level navigation (not inside a single project) under Team > Workload. Capacity per person (hours/day) can be configured individually under their profile in Team Directory.

Title: Setting Up Automations (If This, Then That)
Summary:
Automations let a trigger event automatically perform an action without manual steps. To create one:

  1. Go to Project Settings > Automations.
  2. Click Create Automation.
  3. Choose a trigger (e.g., "Status changes to Done").
  4. Choose an action (e.g., "Notify project owner" or "Move to archive list").
  5. Save and enable the automation — it applies to all tasks in the project going forward, not retroactively to existing tasks.

Title: Creating a Custom Automation Rule
Summary:
Beyond the built-in automation templates, you can build a fully custom rule:

  1. Go to Project Settings > Automations > Create Custom Rule.
  2. Define one or more trigger conditions (field changes, due date approaching, comment added).
  3. Add one or more resulting actions, executed in order.
  4. Optionally add a condition branch (if/else) so different actions fire depending on a field's value.
  5. Test the rule using the built-in preview before enabling it live, to confirm it fires as expected.

Title: Using Tags and Labels
Summary: Tags are freeform labels you can attach to any task for cross-cutting organization that doesn't fit neatly into project or status structure — for example, "urgent," "client-facing," or "needs-design." Add a tag from the task detail panel's Tags field; typing a new tag name creates it workspace-wide for reuse. Tasks can be filtered by tag in any view, and a single task can carry multiple tags simultaneously.

Title: Filtering and Sorting Tasks
Summary: Every view supports filtering by assignee, due date range, status, priority, tag, or any custom field, accessible from the Filter icon above the task list. Multiple filters combine with AND logic by default. Sorting is set independently from filtering, via the Sort icon, and supports sorting by due date, priority, creation date, or alphabetically by task name, in ascending or descending order.

Title: Setting Up Saved Views
Summary: A Saved View captures a specific combination of filters, sort order, and view type (List, Board, etc.) so you don't have to reconfigure it each time. After setting up your filters and sort, click Save as View and give it a name — it now appears as a tab alongside the default views for that project. Saved Views can be marked private (visible only to you) or shared with the whole project team.

Title: Sharing a Project with External Guests
Summary:
To give an external collaborator access without adding them as a full workspace user:

  1. Open the project and click Share.
  2. Enter their email address.
  3. Select Guest as the access level (view and comment only).
  4. Optionally restrict which views or fields are visible to guests.
  5. Send the invite — the guest receives a link to view the shared project without needing a paid seat.

Title: Setting Project-Level Permissions
Summary: Beyond workspace-level roles, individual projects can restrict who can edit versus only view within that specific project, under Project Settings > Permissions. This is useful for sensitive projects (e.g., a compensation planning project) where you want most workspace Members to have no visibility at all, overriding the default that all Members can see all projects. Project-level restrictions never grant more access than a user's workspace-level role allows, only less.

Title: Using the Calendar View
Summary: Calendar view displays tasks by due date in a monthly, weekly, or daily grid, useful for spotting scheduling conflicts and workload clustering. Tasks without a due date don't appear in Calendar view by default, but can be surfaced in an "Unscheduled" sidebar for drag-and-drop scheduling directly onto a date. Calendar view respects the same filters (assignee, tag, status) available in List and Board views.

Title: Syncing Nimbus Workspace with Google Calendar
Summary:
To sync task due dates with your personal Google Calendar:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Integrations > Google Calendar.
  2. Click Connect and complete Google's OAuth consent screen.
  3. Choose which projects' tasks should sync (all projects, or a selected subset).
  4. Choose sync direction: one-way (Nimbus Workspace to Google Calendar) or two-way if you also want date changes made in Google Calendar reflected back.
  5. Save — synced tasks appear as calendar events, refreshing automatically every 15 minutes.

Title: Using Time Tracking on Tasks
Summary: To log time against a task, open it and click the Timer icon to start a live timer, or use Log Time Manually to enter a duration after the fact. Time entries can be tagged as billable or non-billable (Business and Enterprise plans), which feeds into the Time Report for client invoicing or capacity planning. Timers persist across page reloads and continue running until manually stopped, even if you navigate away from the task.

Title: Generating a Project Status Report
Summary: Go to a project's Reports tab and select Status Report to generate a summary of completed vs. remaining tasks, overdue items, and upcoming milestones, formatted for sharing with stakeholders outside the day-to-day project team. Reports can be generated on demand or scheduled to auto-generate and email to a distribution list weekly or monthly. Scheduled reports are a Business and Enterprise feature; on-demand reports are available on all paid plans.

Title: Exporting a Project as PDF
Summary:
To export a shareable snapshot of a project:

  1. Open the project and click the (···) menu.
  2. Select Export > PDF.
  3. Choose which view to export (List, Board, or Gantt) — the PDF renders that view's current layout.
  4. Choose whether to include comments and attachments references.
  5. Click Generate — the PDF downloads once rendering completes, typically within a few seconds for projects under 500 tasks.

Title: Exporting a Project as CSV
Summary:
To export raw task data for spreadsheet analysis or backup:

  1. Open the project and click the (···) menu.
  2. Select Export > CSV.
  3. Choose which fields to include (all fields is the default).
  4. Choose whether to include archived/completed tasks.
  5. Click Export — a CSV file downloads with one row per task, including custom fields as additional columns.

Title: Setting Up Portfolios (Grouping Projects)
Summary: Portfolios (Business and Enterprise) group related projects for roll-up reporting — for example, all projects under a single product launch. Go to workspace-level navigation > Portfolios > Create Portfolio, name it, and add existing projects to it. Portfolio view shows an aggregated timeline and status across all included projects, useful for leadership visibility without opening each project individually. A project can belong to more than one portfolio simultaneously.

Title: Using the Template Gallery
Summary: The Template Gallery (accessible from New Project > Browse Templates) includes both Nimbus Workspace's built-in templates across common categories and any custom templates your own workspace has saved. Templates can be previewed before use, showing their default task lists, custom fields, and views. Business and Enterprise plans can also publish templates to a shared internal gallery visible only within your organization, separate from the public built-in set.

Title: Importing a Project from Asana
Summary:
To migrate an existing Asana project:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Import > Asana.
  2. Authorize Nimbus Workspace to access your Asana account via OAuth.
  3. Select which Asana project(s) to import.
  4. Map Asana custom fields to Nimbus Workspace fields, or let auto-mapping handle common field types.
  5. Click Start Import — task names, assignees, due dates, comments, and attachments are migrated; the import can take several minutes for large projects and you'll get a completion notification.

Title: Importing a Project from Trello
Summary:
To migrate an existing Trello board:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Import > Trello.
  2. Authorize access via Trello's OAuth consent screen.
  3. Select the board(s) to import — Trello lists map to Nimbus Workspace Board columns automatically.
  4. Choose whether to import card checklists as Nimbus Workspace subtasks.
  5. Click Start Import — cards, due dates, labels (mapped to tags), and comments are migrated into a new Nimbus Workspace project.

Title: Setting Up Custom Statuses
Summary: Beyond the default To Do / In Progress / Done statuses, you can define custom ones under Project Settings > Statuses — for example, adding "In Review" or "Blocked." Each custom status can be assigned a color and marked as a "completion" status (counted as done in reports) or not. Reordering statuses here also changes their left-to-right column order in Board view for that project.

Title: Understanding Default Task Statuses
Summary: Every new project starts with three default statuses — To Do, In Progress, and Done — mapped to the standard Board columns and used in default progress reporting. These can be renamed or supplemented with custom statuses, but at least one status must always be marked as a "completion" status for progress percentage calculations to work correctly across List, Board, and reporting views.

Title: Setting a Project Owner
Summary: Every project has one designated Owner, distinct from individual task assignees — the Owner is accountable for the project overall and is the default recipient of project-level notifications like status report generation or an approaching project due date. Set or change the Owner from Project Settings > General > Project Owner; only the current Owner or a workspace Admin can reassign it.

Title: Using @Mentions in Comments
Summary: Type @ followed by a teammate's name in any task comment to notify them directly, regardless of whether they're currently assigned to the task. Mentioned users receive an in-app and (per their notification preferences) email or push notification linking straight to the comment. @mentioning someone in a project they don't yet have access to will prompt you to add them to the project before the mention can be sent.

Title: Attaching Files to Tasks
Summary: Drag and drop a file directly onto a task, or click the paperclip icon in the task detail panel to browse and upload. Individual files are capped at 250MB (500MB on Enterprise); attaching a file counts against your workspace's pooled storage allowance. Files can also be attached by linking a Google Drive or Dropbox file via the respective integration, which doesn't count against your storage allowance since the file remains hosted externally.

Title: Understanding File Storage Limits
Summary: Storage is pooled at the workspace level, not per user: Free includes 2GB, Team 50GB, Business 250GB, and Enterprise is unlimited under a fair-use policy. Storage counts files uploaded directly to Nimbus Workspace; files linked from Google Drive or Dropbox via integration don't count against your allowance since they remain hosted externally. Admins can view current usage under Workspace Settings > Storage, broken down by project.

Title: Setting Up Dark Mode and Display Preferences
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Appearance to switch between Light, Dark, and System (matches your device's OS setting) themes. Display density (Comfortable or Compact) can also be set here, controlling row height and spacing in List view for users who prefer to see more tasks on screen at once. These preferences are personal and don't affect what teammates see when viewing the same project.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Slack
Summary:
To connect Slack:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Integrations > Slack.
  2. Click Connect and authorize the Nimbus Workspace Slack app in your workspace.
  3. Choose a default channel for workspace-wide notifications.
  4. Optionally connect specific projects to specific channels under each project's Integrations tab.
  5. Save — task assignments, due-date reminders, and @mentions can now post to the configured Slack channels, configurable per notification type.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Microsoft Teams
Summary:
To connect Microsoft Teams:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Integrations > Microsoft Teams.
  2. Click Add to Teams and select the target Team and channel.
  3. Authorize the Nimbus Workspace app via Microsoft's consent screen.
  4. Configure which event types (task assignments, comments, due dates) post to the channel.
  5. Save — you can also install the companion Teams tab to view a project's Board directly inside a Teams channel without switching apps.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to GitHub
Summary:
To connect GitHub:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Integrations > GitHub.
  2. Click Connect and authorize the Nimbus Workspace GitHub App on your organization or selected repositories.
  3. Link a repository to a specific Nimbus Workspace project.
  4. Enable Smart Commits so commit messages referencing a task ID (e.g., "Fixes NW-142") automatically update that task's status.
  5. Save — pull request status changes can also be configured to update linked task status automatically.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Jira
Summary:
To connect Jira:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Integrations > Jira.
  2. Click Connect and authenticate with your Atlassian account.
  3. Select the Jira project(s) to link.
  4. Configure field mapping between Jira issue fields and Nimbus Workspace task fields.
  5. Choose one-way sync (Jira to Nimbus Workspace) or two-way sync, then save — two-way sync requires webhook configuration in Jira, detailed in the setup wizard's final step.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Google Drive
Summary:
To connect Google Drive:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Integrations > Google Drive.
  2. Click Connect and complete Google's OAuth consent screen.
  3. Once connected, use Attach from Google Drive on any task instead of uploading a file directly.
  4. Linked files show a live preview and open directly in Google Drive when clicked.
  5. Permissions on the linked file are managed in Google Drive itself — Nimbus Workspace does not change the file's sharing settings.

Title: Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Zapier
Summary:
To connect Zapier:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Integrations > Zapier, or search for "Nimbus Workspace" directly in Zapier's app directory.
  2. Click Connect a New Account and enter your Nimbus Workspace API token when prompted.
  3. Choose a trigger event (e.g., "New Task Created") from the Nimbus Workspace app.
  4. Choose an action in another app (e.g., "Create a row in Google Sheets").
  5. Test the Zap and turn it on — Zapier will poll or receive webhook events depending on the trigger type you selected.

Title: Getting Started with the Nimbus Workspace API
Summary: The Nimbus Workspace REST API (v2) lets you programmatically create, read, update, and delete tasks, projects, and users. Base URL is api.nimbusworkspace.com/v2/. All requests require a Bearer token (a personal access token or OAuth app token) in the Authorization header and return JSON. Full endpoint documentation, including request/response schemas, is available at developers.nimbusworkspace.com. Rate limits apply per token — see the API Rate Limits & Quotas article for details.

Title: Generating a Personal Access Token
Summary:
To create a token for scripts or personal API use:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Developer > Personal Access Tokens.
  2. Click Generate New Token.
  3. Name the token descriptively (e.g., "Reporting Script") and select its scopes (read-only, or read/write).
  4. Set an optional expiration date, or choose Never Expires.
  5. Copy the token immediately — it's shown only once and cannot be retrieved again after leaving the page.

Title: Creating an OAuth App
Summary:
For integrations serving multiple users, register an OAuth app instead of using a personal token:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Developer > OAuth Apps.
  2. Click Register New App.
  3. Enter the app name, redirect URI, and requested scopes.
  4. Save to receive a Client ID and Client Secret.
  5. Implement the standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow using these credentials — the Client Secret should never be embedded in client-side code.

Title: API Rate Limits & Quotas
Summary: Standard API tokens are limited to 100 requests per minute; Enterprise single-tenant API keys are limited to 500 requests per minute. Exceeding your limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying. Rate limits are tracked per token, not per workspace, so multiple integrations using separate tokens have independent quotas. Sustained 429 responses on an Enterprise account after one retry typically indicate a need for a higher negotiated limit — contact Integration Support.

Title: Getting 429 Errors from the API
Summary: A 429 response means you've exceeded your token's rate limit (100 requests/minute standard, 500/minute Enterprise). Check the Retry-After header returned with the error — it tells you exactly how many seconds to wait. Common causes include polling an endpoint too frequently instead of using webhooks for real-time updates, or running parallel scripts that share the same token. Switching high-frequency polling integrations to webhook-based triggers is the most effective fix, since webhooks don't count against your rate limit the way polling requests do.

Title: Understanding API Pagination
Summary: List endpoints (e.g., GET /v2/tasks) return a maximum of 100 records per page by default, up to 250 if explicitly requested via the limit parameter. Each response includes a next_cursor field in its metadata; pass that value as the cursor query parameter on your next request to retrieve the following page. A null next_cursor indicates you've reached the last page. Cursor-based pagination is used rather than page numbers because it remains stable even if records are added or removed between requests.

Title: Understanding API Versioning
Summary: The current stable API version is v2, reflected in the URL path (api.nimbusworkspace.com/v2/). Breaking changes are only introduced in a new major version, never within v2 itself — non-breaking additions (new optional fields, new endpoints) are added to v2 continuously without requiring migration. The legacy v1 API is deprecated but still functional; see the API Deprecation Policy article for the sunset timeline and migration guidance.

Title: API Deprecation Policy
Summary: When an API version or endpoint is deprecated, Nimbus Workspace guarantees a minimum 12-month sunset window before it's disabled, during which the deprecated version continues to function unchanged. Deprecation notices are posted on the developer changelog and emailed to every workspace with an active token calling the deprecated version, at the start of the window and again 90 and 30 days before sunset. The current v1 API is deprecated with a confirmed sunset date published on the developer portal.

Title: Setting Up Webhooks
Summary:
To receive real-time event notifications instead of polling:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Developer > Webhooks.
  2. Click Add Webhook.
  3. Enter your endpoint URL (must be HTTPS) and select which event types to subscribe to (task created, task updated, comment added, etc.).
  4. Save — a webhook secret is generated for verifying payload authenticity.
  5. Use the Send Test Event button to confirm your endpoint receives and correctly acknowledges a sample payload before relying on it in production.

Title: Verifying Webhook Signatures
Summary: Every webhook payload includes an X-Nimbus-Signature header, an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the raw request body signed with your webhook's secret. To verify authenticity, compute the same HMAC over the raw payload using your stored secret and compare it to the header value using a constant-time comparison function — never a simple string equality check, which can leak timing information. Reject any payload whose computed signature doesn't match; this prevents a third party from forging webhook events to your endpoint.

Title: Common Webhook Delivery Failures
Summary: A webhook delivery fails if your endpoint returns anything other than a 2xx status code within 10 seconds, or if the connection times out entirely. Common causes include a misconfigured firewall blocking Nimbus Workspace's IP range, an endpoint returning a 500 error due to unhandled payload fields, or a slow-responding endpoint exceeding the 10-second timeout. Check Workspace Settings > Developer > Webhooks > Delivery Log for the exact response code and latency of recent delivery attempts.

Title: Retrying Failed Webhook Deliveries
Summary: Failed webhook deliveries are automatically retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff (roughly 1, 5, 30, 120, and 600 seconds after the original attempt). After the fifth failure, the event is marked permanently failed and is not retried further, though it remains visible in the Delivery Log for manual inspection. You can manually trigger a one-off redelivery of any logged event, including permanently failed ones, from the Delivery Log's row-level actions menu.

Title: Understanding Webhook Payload Structure
Summary: Every webhook payload is a JSON object with a top-level event_type field (e.g., task.updated), a timestamp, a data object containing the full current state of the affected record, and, for update events, a changes object listing only the fields that changed along with their old and new values. This lets a receiving integration react to the specific change (e.g., only a status change to Done) without needing to diff the full record itself.

Title: Using the Sandbox API Environment
Summary: Enterprise plans include a full sandbox environment (sandbox-api.nimbusworkspace.com) with isolated data, safe for testing integrations without affecting production tasks or triggering real notifications to teammates. Sandbox tokens are generated separately from production tokens under Workspace Settings > Developer > Sandbox, and sandbox data is reset weekly. Webhooks configured in sandbox only fire for sandbox events and never cross over into your production webhook endpoints.

Title: IP Allowlisting for API Access
Summary: Enterprise plans can restrict API token usage to specific IP ranges (e.g., your server's static outbound IP) under Workspace Settings > Developer > API IP Allowlist. Requests from a token configured with an allowlist, arriving from an IP outside that list, are rejected with a 403 error regardless of whether the token itself is valid. This is independent from the account-login IP allowlist described in Restricting Login by IP Address, and applies specifically to API calls.

Title: Understanding OAuth Scopes
Summary: OAuth apps and personal access tokens request specific scopes limiting what they can access — common scopes include tasks:read, tasks:write, projects:read, projects:write, and users:read. Requesting only the minimum scopes your integration actually needs is strongly recommended; a token with tasks:read cannot create or modify tasks even if the underlying token is compromised. Scopes are fixed at token creation and can only be changed by generating a new token with the desired scope set.

Title: Revoking an API Token
