Summary: To revoke a personal access token or OAuth app's access, go to Account Settings > Developer > Personal Access Tokens (or Workspace Settings > Developer > OAuth Apps for an app), find the token or app, and click Revoke. Revocation is immediate — any request using that token fails instantly with a 401 Unauthorized error. Revoking a token does not affect other tokens issued to the same user or app; each token is independent.

Title: Rotating API Credentials
Summary: To rotate a token without downtime, generate a new token with the same scopes before revoking the old one, update your integration or script to use the new token, confirm it's working correctly, and only then revoke the old token. This overlap window avoids an outage that would occur if you revoked first and updated second. Enterprise Client Secrets for OAuth apps can be rotated the same way — Nimbus Workspace supports two active secrets simultaneously during a rotation window.

Title: Rate Limit Headers Explained
Summary: Every API response includes three headers: X-RateLimit-Limit (your token's total requests allowed per minute), X-RateLimit-Remaining (requests left in the current window), and X-RateLimit-Reset (a Unix timestamp for when the window resets). Monitoring X-RateLimit-Remaining proactively, and slowing down before it hits zero, avoids ever receiving a 429 in the first place — this is preferable to a reactive retry-after-429 approach for high-volume integrations.

Title: Bulk Data Export via API
Summary: The GET /v2/export/tasks endpoint generates a full CSV or JSON export of all tasks across specified projects, run asynchronously — the initial call returns a job ID immediately, and you poll GET /v2/export/{job_id}/status until it returns complete with a download URL. This asynchronous pattern is used because full-workspace exports can take several minutes for large accounts and would otherwise exceed typical request timeout limits.

Title: Bulk Data Import via API
Summary: The POST /v2/import/tasks endpoint accepts a batch of up to 500 tasks per request in a single call, validating each row and returning per-row success/failure status rather than failing the entire batch on one bad row. For imports larger than 500 tasks, make sequential batched calls; a common pattern is uploading a CSV client-side, then converting each row into the API's JSON task schema before submitting in batches of 500.

Title: Using the Nimbus Workspace CLI
Summary: The official CLI (installable via npm install -g nimbus-cli) wraps the REST API for common scripting tasks — creating tasks, bulk-tagging, and exporting data from the terminal without writing custom API calls. Authenticate once with nimbus login, which stores a token securely in your local config. Run nimbus --help for the full command list; each command supports a --json flag for scripting output into other tools.

Title: Setting Up a Zapier Trigger
Summary:
To use a Nimbus Workspace event as the trigger for a Zap:

  1. In Zapier, create a new Zap and search for Nimbus Workspace as the trigger app.
  2. Select a trigger event (New Task, Task Completed, New Comment, etc.).
  3. Connect your Nimbus Workspace account if not already connected.
  4. Select which project to watch, or choose all projects.
  5. Test the trigger to pull a sample record, then continue building your Zap's action steps.

Title: Setting Up a Zapier Action
Summary:
To let another app create or update Nimbus Workspace records:

  1. In Zapier, add a new action step and search for Nimbus Workspace.
  2. Select an action event (Create Task, Update Task, Add Comment, etc.).
  3. Connect your Nimbus Workspace account if not already connected.
  4. Map fields from the trigger app's data into the corresponding Nimbus Workspace fields.
  5. Test the action to confirm a record is created or updated correctly, then turn on the Zap.

Title: Two-Way Sync with Jira
Summary: When two-way sync is enabled (see Connecting Nimbus Workspace to Jira), a change made in either system propagates to the other within roughly 60 seconds via webhook, not on a polling delay. Field mapping determines which Jira fields correspond to which Nimbus Workspace fields; unmapped fields on either side are simply ignored during sync rather than causing an error. Conflicting simultaneous edits (both systems changed within the same sync window) are resolved by "last write wins" based on timestamp.

Title: Connecting a Custom Webhook Receiver
Summary: For integrations not covered by a pre-built connector, use the generic Webhooks feature (see Setting Up Webhooks) to POST event data to any HTTPS endpoint you control, then process the payload with your own backend code however you need — updating a database, triggering a Slack message via your own logic, or feeding a custom analytics pipeline. This is the most flexible integration path, at the cost of requiring you to host and maintain the receiving endpoint yourself.

Title: Understanding the REST API Response Format
Summary: Every successful response returns a JSON object with a data field containing the requested resource or array of resources, and a meta field with pagination info where applicable. Error responses return a consistent shape: an error object with a code (e.g., "invalid_scope"), a human-readable message, and, for validation errors, a details array listing the specific field(s) that failed validation, making programmatic error handling straightforward.

Title: Handling API Error Codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 500)
Summary: 400 (Bad Request) indicates malformed input — check the error details array for the specific field. 401 (Unauthorized) means your token is missing, expired, or invalid. 403 (Forbidden) means your token is valid but lacks the required scope, or an IP allowlist blocked the request. 404 (Not Found) means the referenced record ID doesn't exist or you lack access to it. 500 (Internal Server Error) is a Nimbus Workspace-side issue — these are rare and automatically logged for investigation; retrying once after a brief delay is reasonable before contacting support.

Title: Testing API Calls with Postman
Summary: A Postman collection covering every v2 endpoint, with example requests and responses, is available at developers.nimbusworkspace.com/postman. Import the collection, then set a collection-level variable for your personal access token so it's automatically included in every request's Authorization header without re-entering it per call. The collection also includes a pre-configured environment for the sandbox API base URL for Enterprise customers testing against sandbox data.

Title: API Authentication Methods Overview
Summary: Two authentication methods are supported: personal access tokens (simplest, tied to one user, best for scripts and personal automation) and OAuth 2.0 (required for apps used by multiple users or distributed publicly, using the standard authorization code flow). Enterprise customers can additionally request single-tenant API keys, which are not tied to any individual user account and are managed centrally by workspace Admins, useful for service-to-service integrations that shouldn't depend on one employee's account.

Title: Setting Up Single Tenant API Keys for Enterprise
Summary: Enterprise workspaces can request a single-tenant API key, which authenticates as the workspace itself rather than an individual user, so integration access doesn't break if the employee who created a personal token leaves the company. Request one through your customer success manager; keys are provisioned with a higher default rate limit (500 requests/minute) and are managed centrally under Workspace Settings > Developer > Enterprise API Keys, visible only to Admins.

Title: Monitoring API Usage in the Admin Console
Summary: Workspace Settings > Developer > API Usage shows request volume per token over the last 30 days, broken down by endpoint and response status code, helping identify which integration is consuming the most quota or generating an unusual rate of errors. Enterprise plans can set usage alert thresholds here, triggering an email to Admins if any token exceeds a configured percentage of its rate limit sustained over a rolling hour.

Title: Integration Marketplace Overview
Summary: Workspace Settings > Integrations lists every available pre-built connector, organized into categories (Communication, Development, File Storage, Automation, Calendar). Each listing shows required plan tier, a setup difficulty estimate, and a link to detailed setup documentation. Business and Enterprise plans unlock additional premium integrations (deeper Jira two-way sync, advanced Salesforce sync) not available on Team or Free plans.

Title: Disconnecting an Integration
Summary: To remove an integration, go to Workspace Settings > Integrations, find the connected app, and select Disconnect. This immediately revokes the stored OAuth token and stops all future syncing, but does not delete any data that was already synced or created as a result of the integration while it was active — for example, previously posted Slack messages or previously imported Jira tasks remain untouched.

Title: Troubleshooting a Failed Slack Notification
Summary: If Slack notifications stop arriving, first check Workspace Settings > Integrations > Slack for a Reconnect Required badge, which appears if the Slack app's OAuth token was revoked (often due to a Slack workspace admin policy change). If the connection shows healthy, confirm the target channel still exists and the Nimbus Workspace Slack app hasn't been removed from that channel — removing the app from a channel silently stops delivery to it without breaking the overall integration connection.

Title: Syncing Tasks with Outlook Calendar
Summary:
To sync with Outlook Calendar:

  1. Go to Account Settings > Integrations > Outlook Calendar.
  2. Click Connect and complete Microsoft's OAuth consent screen.
  3. Choose which projects' task due dates should sync.
  4. Select one-way or two-way sync.
  5. Save — synced events refresh every 15 minutes and appear in Outlook labeled with the originating Nimbus Workspace project name for easy identification.

Title: Understanding Read vs. Write API Scopes
Summary: Read scopes (e.g., tasks:read) allow retrieving data but never permit creating, updating, or deleting anything, making them the safer default for reporting or monitoring integrations. Write scopes (e.g., tasks:write) allow creating and modifying records and inherently include read access to the same resource type. Always request the narrowest scope combination that satisfies your integration's actual needs — a reporting dashboard, for instance, should never request write scopes.

Title: Data Deletion & GDPR Requests
Summary:
To request deletion of all personal data associated with your account under GDPR Article 17:

  1. Email privacy@nimbusworkspace.com from the email address on file, or ask an Admin to submit the request via Workspace Settings > Privacy > Data Deletion Request.
  2. Nimbus Workspace verifies your identity and organizational authority to make the request.
  3. A confirmation is sent acknowledging receipt within 3 business days.
  4. Deletion is completed within 30 days of a verified request, per our data retention policy.
  5. A final confirmation email is sent once deletion is complete, listing the categories of data removed.

Title: Understanding Nimbus Workspace's Data Retention Policy
Summary: Active workspace data is retained indefinitely while your subscription is active. Deleted tasks and projects remain recoverable in Trash for 30 days before permanent purge. Cancelled workspace data is retained for 90 days post-cancellation to allow reactivation, then permanently purged. Verified GDPR/CCPA deletion requests are honored within 30 days regardless of subscription status, overriding the standard 90-day cancellation retention window.

Title: Exporting Your Workspace Data
Summary:
To export a complete copy of your workspace's data (data portability):

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Privacy > Export My Data.
  2. Select the scope: a single project, all projects, or all data including user directory and audit logs.
  3. Choose the export format (CSV for tabular data, or a full JSON archive).
  4. Click Request Export — large exports are processed asynchronously and you'll receive a download link by email, typically within a few hours.
  5. The download link expires after 7 days for security; re-request if needed.

Title: Importing Data via CSV
Summary:
To bulk-import tasks from an external CSV:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Import > CSV.
  2. Download the field-mapping template to see required column headers.
  3. Prepare your CSV with one task per row, matching the template's columns.
  4. Upload the file and review the field-mapping preview, adjusting any auto-mapped columns that look incorrect.
  5. Click Start Import — you'll get a summary of rows imported successfully versus any that failed validation, with reasons listed per failed row.

Title: Understanding CCPA Opt-Out Requests
Summary: California residents can exercise their CCPA right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information by submitting a request through Workspace Settings > Privacy > CCPA Request, or by emailing privacy@nimbusworkspace.com with "CCPA Opt-Out" in the subject line. Nimbus Workspace does not sell personal information as defined under CCPA in the ordinary course of business; opt-out requests are still honored and confirmed in writing within 15 business days as required by law.

Title: Requesting a Copy of Your Data (Data Portability)
Summary: Under GDPR Article 20 and similar data portability rights, you can request a machine-readable copy of your personal data. Submit the request via Workspace Settings > Privacy > Export My Data, selecting the JSON format for full portability, or contact privacy@nimbusworkspace.com directly if you need a custom scope. This is functionally the same export mechanism used for general workspace backups, but tracked and confirmed as a formal data-subject request when submitted through the Privacy menu.

Title: Understanding Data Residency Options (US vs. EU)
Summary: By default, all workspace data is stored in Nimbus Workspace's US region data centers. Business and Enterprise plans can opt into EU data residency at signup or by request through Support, which stores all workspace data (tasks, files, user records) exclusively in EU-based infrastructure. Data residency cannot be changed after a workspace is created without a full data migration, coordinated with Support, since it involves physically relocating stored data between regions.

Title: Requesting a SOC 2 Report
Summary: Nimbus Workspace maintains a SOC 2 Type II report, renewed annually, covering security, availability, and confidentiality trust principles. Business and Enterprise customers can request the current report under NDA through Workspace Settings > Compliance > Request SOC 2 Report, or via your account executive. The report is typically delivered within 2 business days after the NDA is countersigned through our standard e-signature workflow.

Title: Requesting a Penetration Test Summary
Summary: An executive summary of Nimbus Workspace's most recent third-party penetration test (conducted at least annually) is available to Business and Enterprise customers under NDA, covering methodology and high-level findings without disclosing exploitable technical detail. Request it the same way as the SOC 2 report, through Workspace Settings > Compliance > Request Security Documentation, or through your account executive for Enterprise accounts.

Title: Understanding Nimbus Workspace's Sub-Processor List
Summary: A current list of all third-party sub-processors (cloud infrastructure providers, email delivery services, analytics tools) that may process customer data on Nimbus Workspace's behalf is published at nimbusworkspace.com/subprocessors and updated whenever a new sub-processor is added. Enterprise customers with a signed Data Processing Agreement can subscribe to email notifications of sub-processor changes, with a minimum 30-day notice before a new sub-processor begins processing their data.

Title: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) Overview
Summary: Nimbus Workspace's standard Data Processing Agreement, compliant with GDPR Article 28 requirements, is available to all Business and Enterprise customers and can be countersigned electronically through Workspace Settings > Compliance > Data Processing Agreement without needing to involve an account executive. Enterprise customers requiring custom DPA terms (specific sub-processor restrictions, custom audit rights) should route the request through Legal via their account executive instead of the self-serve flow.

Title: Understanding Backup and Restore Policy
Summary: Nimbus Workspace performs automated encrypted backups of all workspace data every 24 hours, retained for 35 days on a rolling basis. Backups are used for disaster recovery (restoring service after an infrastructure failure) and are not directly customer-accessible as a self-service restore point — for accidental data loss within your own workspace, use the 30-day Trash recovery window instead, which is faster and self-service.

Title: Exporting an Audit Trail
Summary: Business and Enterprise plans include an audit log tracking security-relevant events (logins, permission changes, data exports, integration connections). To export it, go to Workspace Settings > Security > Audit Log, apply any date-range or event-type filters, and click Export CSV. Audit log entries are retained for 12 months by default; Enterprise customers can request an extended retention period of up to 7 years for regulatory compliance.

Title: Understanding the Audit Log Feature
Summary: The audit log records who did what and when for security-sensitive actions: logins (including failed attempts), role changes, user deactivation, data exports, integration connections/disconnections, and changes to security settings like SSO or IP allowlisting. Regular task and project activity (creating a task, changing its status) is not part of the security audit log — that's tracked separately in each task's own activity history, viewable from the task detail panel.

Title: Setting a Custom Data Retention Schedule (Enterprise)
Summary: Enterprise customers with specific regulatory retention requirements can configure a custom retention schedule (e.g., auto-purge completed tasks after 3 years) under Workspace Settings > Compliance > Retention Schedule. This is configured jointly with Nimbus Workspace's compliance team to ensure the schedule doesn't conflict with active legal holds, and typically requires a brief onboarding call to confirm the specific regulatory framework driving the requirement.

Title: Deleting a Workspace and Its Data
Summary: See Closing Your Nimbus Workspace Account for the full closure procedure. From a compliance standpoint: closure queues all workspace data for permanent deletion within 30 days, consistent with standard retention policy, and this cannot be expedited faster than 30 days even upon request, since it aligns with our standard secure-deletion verification process across backup systems.

Title: Understanding What Happens to Data After Cancellation
Summary: Cancelling a subscription (converting to Free plan) is distinct from closing the workspace entirely — cancellation retains all data for 90 days in case you reactivate, with anything over Free plan limits (extra seats, storage, premium integrations) becoming read-only rather than deleted. Only a full workspace closure, a separate and explicit action, queues data for permanent deletion, and that happens within 30 days rather than 90.

Title: Requesting Data Deletion for a Departed Employee
Summary:
To remove a specific former employee's personal data (rather than closing the whole workspace) under GDPR/CCPA:

  1. Have a workspace Admin deactivate the user first via Team Directory, if not already done.
  2. Submit a Data Deletion Request via Workspace Settings > Privacy, specifying the individual user rather than the full account.
  3. Nimbus Workspace verifies the request comes from an authorized Admin.
  4. Personal identifying information is removed and historical records are reattributed to "Former User" within 30 days.
  5. Task content and comments they authored remain (as workspace business records) unless separately flagged for removal.

Title: Bulk Exporting Attachments and Files
Summary: To export all files attached across your workspace (not just task data), go to Workspace Settings > Privacy > Export My Data, select Include Attachments, and choose Full JSON Archive as the format. Large workspaces with many files may take several hours to package; you'll receive a download link by email once ready, valid for 7 days, delivered as a single compressed archive organized by project folder.

Title: Understanding HIPAA Applicability
Summary: Nimbus Workspace is not designed or certified for storing Protected Health Information (PHI) and does not sign Business Associate Agreements for standard Team or Business plans. Enterprise customers in healthcare-adjacent industries who need to discuss HIPAA-aligned controls or a BAA should contact their account executive — support for regulated healthcare data requires specific contractual and technical arrangements evaluated on a case-by-case basis, not available as a standard feature.

Title: Understanding Data Encryption at Rest and in Transit
Summary: All data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; all data in transit between your browser or API client and Nimbus Workspace's servers is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher, with older TLS versions rejected outright. Encryption keys are managed through a dedicated key management service with automatic annual rotation. This applies uniformly across all plan tiers — encryption is not an Enterprise-only feature.

Title: Configuring Data Loss Prevention Settings
Summary: Enterprise plans support basic Data Loss Prevention controls under Workspace Settings > Compliance > DLP, including restricting file attachment types, disabling external sharing/guest access workspace-wide, and blocking bulk export for non-Admin roles. These controls are additive restrictions on top of standard role permissions — they can only make the workspace more restrictive, not grant additional access beyond what a role already allows.

Title: Understanding Cross-Border Data Transfer Safeguards
Summary: For customers whose data is processed across regions (for example, a US-headquartered company with EU-based team members on a US-region workspace), Nimbus Workspace relies on Standard Contractual Clauses incorporated into our Data Processing Agreement as the transfer safeguard mechanism, consistent with current GDPR guidance following the invalidation of prior transfer frameworks. Customers requiring data to remain strictly within one region should use the EU Data Residency option instead of relying on transfer safeguards.

Title: Requesting an Incident History Report
Summary: A history of any past security incidents affecting customer data (if any) that met the disclosure threshold under our incident response policy is available to Business and Enterprise customers on request through Workspace Settings > Compliance > Security Documentation. Material incidents affecting a specific customer's data are also proactively disclosed directly to that customer's Admins, separate from this on-request historical summary.

Title: Understanding the Status Page and Uptime SLA
Summary: Real-time system status and historical uptime is published at status.nimbusworkspace.com, including incident post-mortems for any outage affecting core functionality. Business and Enterprise contracts include a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA with defined service credits for shortfalls, detailed in the Master Service Agreement. Subscribe to status.nimbusworkspace.com directly for email or SMS alerts on new incidents, independent of your Nimbus Workspace login.

Title: Reviewing the Subprocessor Change Notification Policy
Summary: Enterprise customers with a signed DPA can opt into advance email notification whenever a new sub-processor is added to Nimbus Workspace's published sub-processor list, with a minimum 30-day notice before the new sub-processor begins processing data, giving time to object per the DPA's objection procedure if needed. Opt in under Workspace Settings > Compliance > Sub-Processor Notifications; this is off by default and must be explicitly enabled per workspace.

Title: Setting Up Legal Hold on a Workspace
Summary: Enterprise customers involved in litigation or a regulatory investigation can request a Legal Hold on specific projects or the entire workspace, which suspends the standard data retention and deletion schedule (including the 30-day Trash purge) for the held scope until the hold is lifted. Legal Holds are configured jointly with Nimbus Workspace's Legal team — request one through your account executive, providing the scope and expected duration if known.

Title: Exporting Data for eDiscovery
Summary: For eDiscovery requests, Enterprise customers can request a comprehensive export including task content, comments, attachments, and full audit log history within a specified date range, formatted for legal review platforms. This differs from the standard self-service export in that it includes deleted/archived items still within retention and is fulfilled directly by Nimbus Workspace's compliance team rather than the self-service Export My Data flow — request it through your account executive or privacy@nimbusworkspace.com.

Title: Understanding Consent Management for Guest Users
Summary: Guest users invited to a shared project are shown a brief consent notice on first access, describing what data (their name, email, and any comments they post) will be visible to the inviting workspace. Guests can decline and are not granted access if they do not consent. Workspace Admins can review a log of guest consent events under Workspace Settings > Privacy > Guest Consent Log.

Title: Data Minimization Practices at Nimbus Workspace
Summary: Nimbus Workspace collects only the data needed to provide the service — account profile information, task/project content you create, and standard operational logs (login times, API usage) needed for security and billing. We do not sell personal data or use customer task content to train shared AI models without explicit opt-in; any AI features process content in the context of your own workspace only.

Title: Understanding Cookie and Tracking Policy
Summary: Nimbus Workspace uses essential cookies required for login sessions and security (cannot be disabled without breaking core functionality) and optional analytics cookies used to understand product usage patterns, which can be disabled from the cookie consent banner or later under Account Settings > Privacy > Cookie Preferences. A full list of cookies in use, their purpose, and retention period is published at nimbusworkspace.com/cookie-policy.

Title: Requesting Account Data Anonymization
Summary: As an alternative to full deletion, you can request anonymization of your personal data instead — your name and email are replaced with a generic identifier across historical records (comments, task assignments) while preserving the business record itself for workspace continuity. Request this via privacy@nimbusworkspace.com, specifying anonymization rather than deletion; note this is irreversible, same as deletion, once processed.

Title: Understanding Children's Data Policy (COPPA)
Summary: Nimbus Workspace is a business productivity tool intended for users 16 years of age or older and is not directed at children; we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 in a manner requiring COPPA compliance. If we become aware that a child's data has been collected without appropriate consent, it is deleted promptly upon verification — report any such concern to privacy@nimbusworkspace.com.

Title: Reviewing the Acceptable Use Policy
Summary: The Acceptable Use Policy, published at nimbusworkspace.com/aup, prohibits using Nimbus Workspace to store or transmit illegal content, malware, or content that infringes third-party intellectual property, and prohibits attempts to circumvent rate limits, security controls, or seat-based billing through technical workarounds. Violations can result in content removal, account suspension, or termination depending on severity, as outlined in the full policy.

Title: Understanding the Privacy Shield / Data Transfer Framework Status
Summary: Following the evolution of EU-US data transfer frameworks, Nimbus Workspace relies primarily on Standard Contractual Clauses (incorporated in our DPA) as the mechanism for lawful cross-border transfer, and additionally participates in the current EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where applicable as a supplementary safeguard. Current certification status is published at nimbusworkspace.com/data-transfer and updated as the regulatory landscape evolves.

Title: Setting Data Export Permissions for Admins Only
Summary: By default, any Member can export the projects they have access to. Business and Enterprise Admins can restrict bulk data export (CSV/JSON export of tasks or the full workspace) to Admin and Owner roles only, under Workspace Settings > Compliance > DLP > Restrict Data Export. This does not affect individual file downloads (opening a single attachment), only bulk export functionality.

Title: Scheduling Automated Data Exports
Summary:
To set up a recurring backup export without manually triggering it each time:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Privacy > Scheduled Exports.
  2. Click Create Scheduled Export.
  3. Choose the scope (all projects, or a specific subset) and format (CSV or JSON).
  4. Set a frequency: daily, weekly, or monthly.
  5. Choose delivery: email link, or (Enterprise) automatic delivery to a connected S3 bucket or SFTP endpoint for long-term archival outside Nimbus Workspace.

Title: Understanding Retention of Deleted Tasks and Projects
Summary: Deleted tasks and projects move to Trash and remain recoverable for exactly 30 days, after which they are permanently purged from both production storage and, within an additional 35 days, from the encrypted backup rotation as well. There is no way to recover data past the 30-day Trash window through self-service or Support — this window is intentionally firm to keep the stated retention policy accurate and auditable.

Title: Requesting a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
Summary: As noted under Understanding HIPAA Applicability, Nimbus Workspace does not offer a standard BAA for Team or Business plans. Enterprise customers in healthcare-adjacent contexts who believe they need a BAA should raise this with their account executive early in the sales process, since it requires a dedicated technical and contractual review to confirm whether Nimbus Workspace's current architecture can support the required safeguards for that specific use case.

Title: Understanding Log Retention for Security Events
Summary: Security-relevant logs (login attempts, authentication events, admin actions) are retained for 12 months by default across all plans, and are the basis for the Audit Log feature. Enterprise customers can request extended retention up to 7 years for regulatory purposes, configured under Workspace Settings > Compliance > Retention Schedule alongside other custom retention settings.

Title: Migrating Data Between Workspaces
Summary:
To move projects from one Nimbus Workspace account to another (for example, after a company divestiture):

  1. Export the source workspace's data using Export My Data with the Full JSON Archive format.
  2. Have an Admin on the destination workspace go to Workspace Settings > Import > Nimbus Workspace Archive.
  3. Upload the exported archive file.
  4. Map any users who should be re-invited to the destination workspace versus left unassigned.
  5. Start the import — this is a copy operation, so the source workspace's data is unaffected and remains until you separately choose to delete or archive it there.

Title: Understanding the Right to Rectification Process
Summary: Under GDPR Article 16 and similar rights, you can request correction of inaccurate personal data held about you. Most profile information (name, email, job title) can be corrected directly under Account Settings > Profile without a formal request. For data you cannot self-correct (for example, historical audit log entries), submit a request to privacy@nimbusworkspace.com describing the inaccuracy; corrections to historical records are evaluated case by case to balance accuracy against record-integrity requirements.

Title: Mobile App Troubleshooting
Summary:
If the mobile app is behaving unexpectedly, work through these steps in order:

  1. Confirm you're on the latest app version from the App Store or Google Play — many issues are fixed in the most recent release.
  2. Force-close the app completely and reopen it.
  3. Check your internet connection; switch between Wi-Fi and cellular data to isolate a network-specific issue.
  4. Log out and log back in to refresh your session.
  5. If the issue persists, reinstall the app entirely — this clears any corrupted local cache without affecting your account data, which is stored server-side.

Title: Mobile App Keeps Crashing on iOS
Summary:
For repeated crashes specifically on iOS:

  1. Confirm your iOS version is 16 or later — older versions are no longer supported by the current app build.
  2. Update the Nimbus Workspace app from the App Store to the latest version.
  3. Restart your iPhone or iPad completely (not just the app).
  4. Free up storage space — iOS can terminate apps abnormally when device storage is critically low.
  5. If crashes continue, delete and reinstall the app, then report the crash to Support with your device model and iOS version for investigation.

Title: Mobile App Keeps Crashing on Android
Summary:
For repeated crashes specifically on Android:

  1. Confirm your Android version is 10 or later.
  2. Update the app via Google Play to the latest version.
  3. Go to Android Settings > Apps > Nimbus Workspace > Storage and clear the app cache (not app data, which would log you out).
  4. Restart your device.
  5. If crashes continue, note your exact device model and Android version and contact Support — some crashes are manufacturer-specific and require targeted investigation.

Title: Nimbus Workspace Won't Load in Chrome
Summary: If the app fails to load or shows a blank page in Chrome, clear your browser cache and cookies for nimbusworkspace.com specifically (Settings > Privacy > Clear Browsing Data, scoped to this site), then reload. Disable browser extensions one at a time, particularly ad blockers or script blockers, since these occasionally block required assets. Confirm you're on a supported Chrome version (the current version or one major version behind). If the issue persists across a different browser too, it's likely network- or account-related rather than browser-specific — contact Support.

Title: Fixing a Blank Screen After Login
Summary: A blank screen immediately after login is most commonly a stale cached JavaScript bundle conflicting with a recent app update. Try a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) before anything else. If that doesn't resolve it, clear your browser's cache for the site and reload. Check status.nimbusworkspace.com for any active incident affecting page load. If the blank screen persists after these steps, try an incognito/private window to rule out a corrupted local session.

Title: Notifications Not Showing Up
Summary: First confirm your notification preferences under Account Settings > Notifications haven't been narrowed to exclude the event type you expected (task assignment, mention, etc.). Check that Do Not Disturb isn't currently active. On mobile, confirm push notifications are enabled both in the Nimbus Workspace app settings and at the OS level (iOS Settings > Notifications, or Android equivalent) — an OS-level permission revoked outside the app silently blocks delivery without any error shown in-app.

Title: Email Notifications Not Being Received
Summary: If email notifications aren't arriving, check your spam or junk folder first — automated notification emails are occasionally filtered by aggressive corporate spam filters. Confirm your notification preferences under Account Settings > Notifications have email enabled for the relevant event type. If your organization uses an email allowlist, ask IT to allowlist notifications@nimbusworkspace.com. If only some notification types are missing while others arrive normally, the issue is almost always a preference setting rather than a delivery problem.

Title: Slow Performance on Large Projects
Summary: Projects with several thousand tasks can experience slower List or Board view rendering, particularly with many custom fields displayed simultaneously. To improve performance: apply a filter to reduce the visible task count, hide unused custom field columns, and consider archiving completed tasks older than a defined threshold rather than keeping them in the active view indefinitely. Gantt view is the most performance-sensitive view for very large projects; List view with filters applied is typically fastest for day-to-day work on large projects.

Title: Files Won't Upload
Summary: If a file upload fails, first confirm it's under the 250MB size limit (500MB on Enterprise) — oversized files fail silently in some browsers rather than showing a clear error. Check your internet connection stability, since large uploads that lose connection partway don't automatically resume. Confirm the file type isn't blocked by a workspace-level Data Loss Prevention restriction on attachment types, if your organization has one configured. Try a different browser to rule out a browser-specific upload handling issue.

Title: Comments Not Saving
Summary: If a comment appears to submit but doesn't persist after refresh, this is most often a network interruption during submission — check for a brief "Sending..." indicator that never resolves to "Sent," which confirms a connectivity issue rather than a bug. Try again on a stable connection. If comments consistently fail to save even on a stable connection, clear your browser cache, since a stale cached version of the app can occasionally mishandle the comment submission request format after an update.

Title: Task Assignment Not Working
Summary: If assigning a task to a teammate doesn't seem to take effect, confirm the person is actually a member of that specific project — you cannot assign a task to someone without project access, and the assignee dropdown will only show valid candidates, though occasionally a cached member list can show someone who was since removed. Refresh the page to reload the current member list, then try the assignment again. If the assignee field reverts to unassigned after saving, check whether an automation rule on the project is unintentionally clearing the assignee field on certain triggers.

Title: Calendar Sync Not Updating
Summary: If Google or Outlook Calendar isn't reflecting recent Nimbus Workspace task changes, remember sync runs on a 15-minute refresh interval, not instantly — wait at least that long before troubleshooting further. If it's been longer than 15 minutes, check Account Settings > Integrations for a Reconnect Required badge, which appears if the calendar provider's access token expired or was revoked. Reconnecting re-authorizes access and typically resolves a stalled sync immediately on the next scheduled run.

Title: Search Not Returning Expected Results
Summary: Nimbus Workspace search indexes task titles, descriptions, and comments, but newly created or edited content can take up to 2 minutes to appear in search results due to indexing delay — this is expected, not a bug. Confirm you're searching within the correct scope (a single project versus workspace-wide, toggled at the top of the search results panel). If a specific task never appears in search even after several minutes, confirm you actually have access to the project it belongs to, since search never surfaces content you can't otherwise view.

Title: Gantt Chart Not Rendering Correctly
Summary: Gantt rendering issues (overlapping bars, missing dependency lines) are most often caused by tasks with conflicting or missing dates — a task with a due date earlier than its start date, for example, can render unpredictably. Review tasks flagged with a date-conflict warning icon in List view and correct their start/due dates. If the chart still renders incorrectly after fixing date conflicts, try a hard browser refresh, since Gantt view caches layout calculations client-side for performance.

Title: Automation Rule Not Triggering
Summary: If an automation doesn't fire as expected, first confirm it's actually enabled — automations can be toggled off without being deleted, and a disabled rule shows greyed out under Project Settings > Automations. Next, verify the trigger condition precisely matches what you did (for example, a trigger set to "Status changes to Done" won't fire if you deleted the task instead of completing it). Automations also don't run retroactively on existing tasks — they only fire on changes that happen after the automation was enabled.

Title: Time Tracking Timer Not Stopping
Summary: If a time tracking timer appears stuck running, it may simply be running on a different device or browser tab than the one you're currently viewing — timers are tied to your account, not a specific device, and only one can run at a time per user. Check Account Settings > Time Tracking > Active Timer to see and stop it from any device. If a timer shows as running but you're certain you stopped it earlier, refresh the page — this is typically a display caching issue rather than the timer actually still running server-side.

Title: Unable to Drag and Drop Tasks
Summary: Drag-and-drop reordering (in Board or List view) requires JavaScript to be fully loaded and can fail silently if a browser extension is interfering with pointer events — try disabling extensions, particularly ad blockers, one at a time. Drag-and-drop is also disabled for users with Guest-level access, by design, since guests cannot modify project structure. Confirm your role has edit permission on the project if reordering consistently fails only in one specific project.

Title: Offline Mode Not Syncing Changes
Summary: Changes made in the mobile app while offline are queued locally and sync automatically once connectivity returns — this can take up to a minute after reconnecting, not instantly. If changes still haven't synced after several minutes on a confirmed stable connection, open the app's Sync Status screen (Settings > Sync Status) to see any pending items and their error state. A sync conflict (the same task edited both offline and by someone else online) will show a manual resolution prompt rather than silently discarding either version.

Title: App Stuck on Loading Screen
Summary: If the app hangs indefinitely on its initial loading screen, check status.nimbusworkspace.com first for an active incident. If status is normal, force-close and reopen the app (mobile) or hard-refresh the browser tab (web). Confirm your device's date and time are set correctly and set to automatic — an incorrect system clock can cause authentication token validation to fail silently, presenting as a stuck loading state rather than a clear error message.

Title: Login Loop After Entering Password
Summary: A login loop (returning to the login page repeatedly after a seemingly successful password entry) is most often caused by third-party cookies being blocked in your browser, which breaks the session token handoff. Enable cookies for nimbusworkspace.com specifically, or check your browser's tracking-prevention settings if using Safari or Firefox in a strict privacy mode. If you're on an SSO-enabled workspace, a login loop can also indicate a misconfigured identity provider assertion — contact your workspace Admin to review the SSO configuration.

Title: Two-Factor Authentication Code Not Working
Summary: If your 2FA code is rejected, first confirm your device's clock is set to automatic network time — TOTP codes are time-based and even a few minutes of drift will produce an invalid code. Confirm you're reading the current code and not one that already expired (codes rotate every 30 seconds). If using SMS-based 2FA, confirm you have signal and haven't blocked the sending number. If none of these resolve it, use a saved backup code to log in, then re-set up 2FA from scratch.

Title: Browser Compatibility Issues
Summary: Nimbus Workspace officially supports the current and previous major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Internet Explorer is not supported and will show a persistent compatibility warning banner. If you experience layout glitches or broken functionality, first confirm your browser version meets the minimum supported version before troubleshooting further, since older unsupported browser versions are the most common root cause of otherwise-unexplained rendering issues.

Title: Dark Mode Display Glitches
Summary: Occasional color-contrast or icon-visibility glitches in Dark Mode are usually resolved by a hard refresh, which reloads the current theme's stylesheet cleanly. If a specific custom field type or third-party embedded content (like a linked Google Drive file preview) doesn't render correctly in Dark Mode, this is a known limitation for a small number of embed types rather than a bug in your specific workspace — switching to Light Mode is the current workaround for those specific embeds.

Title: Keyboard Shortcuts Not Responding
Summary: Keyboard shortcuts are disabled while a text field (like a task description or comment box) has focus, by design, to avoid conflicting with normal typing — click outside any input field before using a shortcut. Confirm no browser extension is intercepting the same key combination (common with certain shortcut-manager or vim-emulation extensions). The full shortcut list is viewable in-app by pressing ? (Shift+/), which also confirms whether shortcuts are functioning at all.

Title: Duplicate Notifications Being Sent
Summary: Duplicate notifications for the same event are most often caused by having the same notification type enabled across multiple channels (email, in-app, and mobile push) without realizing each fires independently for the same underlying event — this is expected behavior, not a bug, and can be adjusted under Account Settings > Notifications by disabling redundant channels. True duplicate notifications within the same channel (two identical emails) typically indicate an automation rule that's configured to trigger on the same condition more than once — review Project Settings > Automations for overlapping rules.

Title: Missing Tasks After Import
Summary: If tasks appear missing after a CSV or Asana/Trello import, first check the import summary report (available from Workspace Settings > Import > Import History) for any rows flagged as failed — these are the most common reason for a lower-than-expected task count, and the report lists the specific validation reason per failed row (commonly a missing required field or an invalid date format). Also confirm you're viewing the correct project; large imports occasionally get mapped to an unintended target project if it wasn't explicitly selected during setup.

Title: Export Getting Stuck or Timing Out
Summary: Large exports (thousands of tasks with attachments) are processed asynchronously and can take up to a few hours — this is expected, not a failure, and you'll receive an email with the download link once ready rather than needing to wait on the page. If an export has been pending for more than 24 hours with no completion email, check Workspace Settings > Privacy > Export My Data for its status; a status of Failed rather than Processing indicates a genuine issue, at which point contact Support with the export request timestamp.

Title: Integration Sync Delay with Slack
Summary: Slack notifications typically post within seconds of the triggering event. A sustained delay (more than a minute) usually indicates Slack-side rate limiting on their Events API, which self-resolves without any action needed on your end. If delays persist beyond 10 minutes consistently, check Workspace Settings > Integrations > Slack for a connection health warning, and confirm the Nimbus Workspace Slack app hasn't been rate-limited at the Slack workspace level by an overly aggressive third-party Slack app also installed there.

Title: Webhook Not Firing After Task Update
Summary: If a configured webhook isn't firing, first confirm the webhook is enabled and subscribed to the correct event type under Workspace Settings > Developer > Webhooks — a webhook subscribed only to task.created won't fire on an update. Check the Delivery Log for the specific event; if it shows as attempted but failed, review the returned status code, since your endpoint must return a 2xx response within 10 seconds for delivery to be marked successful (see Common Webhook Delivery Failures for detail).

Title: Custom Field Values Disappearing
Summary: A custom field value that appears to disappear is most often actually just hidden from the current view via the Fields visibility toggle (see Customizing Task Fields) rather than genuinely cleared — check whether the field is simply hidden before assuming data loss. If a Dropdown-type custom field's value is genuinely blank, confirm the previously selected option wasn't deleted from the field's configuration, since removing a dropdown option clears it from any task that had it selected.

Title: Unable to Delete a Project
Summary: If Delete Project is greyed out or fails, confirm your role has delete permission — only Admins and the designated Project Owner can delete a project by default. A project under an active Legal Hold (Enterprise) cannot be deleted until the hold is lifted, regardless of role, and will show a specific Legal Hold notice rather than a generic permission error. If you have the correct role and no hold applies, try archiving first (a lesser action) to confirm basic project-modification permissions are working at all.

Title: Guest User Can't Access Shared Project
Summary: If an invited guest reports they can't access a shared project, first confirm the invite was actually accepted — a pending invitation grants no access until accepted, visible under Team Directory > Pending Invitations. Confirm the guest is using the same email address the invite was sent to; a guest attempting to log in with a different email won't be recognized as the invited user. Also confirm the project's sharing settings weren't since revoked under Project Settings > Permissions.

Title: Video/Screen Recording Attachments Won't Play
Summary: Video attachments over 250MB will fail to upload rather than fail to play — confirm the file was fully uploaded first by checking it shows a complete thumbnail rather than a processing spinner. For videos that uploaded successfully but won't play, confirm the file format is one of the supported types (MP4, MOV, WebM); other formats will display as a downloadable file rather than an inline player, which is expected behavior rather than a playback bug.

Title: Push Notifications Not Working on Mobile
Summary: Confirm push notifications are enabled at both the app level (Nimbus Workspace app Settings > Notifications) and the OS level (device Settings > Notifications > Nimbus Workspace) — an OS-level permission revoked outside the app silently blocks all push delivery with no in-app error shown. On iOS, also confirm Focus modes or Do Not Disturb aren't suppressing notifications system-wide. Reinstalling the app re-triggers the OS notification permission prompt if it was previously dismissed without granting access.

Title: App Freezing When Switching Views
Summary: Occasional brief freezing when switching between List, Board, and Gantt views on a very large project (several thousand tasks) is a known performance characteristic tied to view re-rendering, not a bug — applying a filter to reduce visible task count before switching views significantly improves this. Persistent freezing on smaller projects, or freezing that doesn't resolve after a few seconds, is not expected — try a hard browser refresh, and if it recurs, contact Support with the specific project size and view combination.

Title: Recurring Task Creating Duplicates
Summary: If a recurring task is generating more than one new instance per cycle, check whether the recurrence rule was accidentally set up twice — opening the original task's due date field will show if Make Recurring was applied more than once, which can happen if a browser tab was left open and the action submitted twice. Remove the duplicate recurrence rule, keeping only one, and delete any already-generated duplicate instances manually; this won't affect the correctly configured recurrence going forward.

Title: Wrong Time Zone Displayed on Due Dates
Summary: Due dates display in each individual user's own profile time zone setting (Account Settings > Profile > Time Zone), not the workspace default or the time zone of whoever created the task — this is by design so a global team each sees accurate local deadlines, but it means two people can correctly see the same due date rendered at different clock times. Confirm your personal profile time zone is set correctly before assuming a display bug.

Title: Unable to Reorder Subtasks
Summary: Subtask reordering uses the same drag-and-drop mechanism as top-level tasks, and is subject to the same permission requirement — Guest-level access cannot reorder subtasks, by design. If you have edit permission and reordering still doesn't work, confirm you're dragging by the subtask's designated drag handle icon rather than clicking directly on the subtask text, which instead opens the subtask for editing rather than initiating a drag.

Title: Template Not Applying Correctly
Summary: If a project created from a template is missing expected structure (custom fields, saved views), confirm the template itself still has that structure — templates can be edited after creation, and a project created from an older version of a template won't retroactively pick up later template changes. If a genuinely current template applies incompletely, try recreating the project from the template again; a partial application usually indicates a page was closed mid-creation rather than a persistent template defect.

Title: SSO Login Failing After Password Change
Summary: On an SSO-enabled workspace, your Nimbus Workspace password is not used for login at all — authentication happens entirely through your identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, etc.). If login fails after changing a password, confirm you changed it with your identity provider (IT department), not through any Nimbus Workspace password field, since Nimbus Workspace-side password resets have no effect on SSO-enforced accounts. Contact your IT team if the identity provider password change itself is the issue.

Title: Report Data Doesn't Match Dashboard
Summary: A discrepancy between a generated Status Report and a live dashboard view is usually a timing difference — reports capture a point-in-time snapshot at generation, while dashboards reflect live data that may have changed since. Regenerate the report to compare against current dashboard data rather than assuming a calculation error. If numbers still don't reconcile after regenerating, confirm both are scoped to the same filter set (e.g., the report excluding archived tasks while the dashboard includes them, or vice versa).

Title: High CPU Usage from Desktop App
Summary: Sustained high CPU usage from the desktop app is most commonly caused by a very large project's Gantt view being left open in the background, which continues background layout calculations. Closing unused project tabs, especially Gantt views, typically resolves it immediately. If high CPU usage persists even with no large projects open, try fully quitting and relaunching the desktop app, and confirm you're on the latest version, since performance fixes are shipped regularly.

Title: Unable to Print a Project View
Summary: Printing directly from the browser's print function can render Board and Gantt views poorly, since they're not optimized for print layout — use Export > PDF instead (see Exporting a Project as PDF), which generates a print-optimized layout specifically designed for physical printing or PDF distribution, rather than relying on the browser's generic print-to-PDF handling of the live interactive view.

Title: Error Message: "Something Went Wrong" on Save
Summary: This generic error indicates the save request failed server-side without a more specific reason surfaced to the client, typically due to a brief connectivity blip or a temporary server-side issue. First, retry the save once — most instances resolve on retry. If it recurs specifically when saving a particular field or task, note the exact field and try a hard browser refresh before retrying again. If the error persists across multiple attempts and tasks, check status.nimbusworkspace.com, then contact Support with the approximate time of the failed save.

Title: Account Security & Suspicious Activity
Summary:
If you notice a login from an unfamiliar location or device in your login notifications:

  1. Change your password immediately from Account Settings > Security.
  2. Go to Active Sessions and click Sign Out of All Devices to terminate any unauthorized session.
  3. Enable Two-Factor Authentication if it isn't already on.
  4. Review the Audit Log (Business/Enterprise) for any changes made during the suspicious session.
  5. Contact Security Support at security@nimbusworkspace.com if you believe your account data was accessed or altered without authorization.

Title: What to Do If You See an Unrecognized Login
Summary: An unrecognized-login email notification includes the approximate location, device type, and time of the sign-in. If you don't recognize it, change your password right away and review Active Sessions to revoke it directly. If you do recognize the login but simply didn't expect the notification (a new device, a VPN changing your apparent location), no action is needed — this notification is a routine security measure, not necessarily a sign of compromise.

Title: Setting Up Login Alerts
Summary:
Login alert emails for new devices or locations are enabled by default and cannot be fully disabled for individual users, since they're a core account-security feature. Business and Enterprise Admins can additionally configure alerts to also copy a shared security inbox for all workspace logins, under Workspace Settings > Security > Login Alerts:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Security > Login Alerts.
  2. Toggle on Copy Admins on New Device Logins.
  3. Select which Admin roles receive the copy.
  4. Optionally set a threshold (e.g., only alert on logins from a new country, not just a new device).
  5. Save — alerts apply to all users workspace-wide going forward.

Title: Understanding Nimbus Workspace's Security Architecture
Summary: Nimbus Workspace is built on a multi-tenant cloud architecture with logical data isolation per workspace, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and role-based access control enforced at the API layer for every request, not just the UI. Infrastructure runs on a major cloud provider with SOC 2-compliant data centers. A detailed architecture overview is available to Business and Enterprise customers under NDA — request it via Workspace Settings > Compliance > Security Documentation.

Title: Reporting a Security Vulnerability
Summary: If you discover a potential security vulnerability, report it responsibly to security@nimbusworkspace.com with as much detail as possible (steps to reproduce, affected component, potential impact) rather than testing further against production data or disclosing it publicly. Nimbus Workspace acknowledges reports within 24 hours and provides regular status updates until resolution, consistent with our published Responsible Disclosure Policy.

Title: Understanding the Bug Bounty Program
Summary: Nimbus Workspace runs a bug bounty program for qualifying security researchers, with reward tiers based on severity (using a standard CVSS-based scoring approach) and scope limited to production systems explicitly listed in the program's published rules at nimbusworkspace.com/security/bug-bounty. Testing against other customers' live data, denial-of-service testing, and social engineering are explicitly out of scope and excluded from reward eligibility.

Title: Enforcing 2FA Organization-Wide
Summary:
Business and Enterprise Admins can require all users to enable 2FA rather than leaving it optional:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication.
  2. Toggle on Require 2FA for All Users.
  3. Set a grace period (recommended: 7 days) during which users are prompted but not yet blocked.
  4. After the grace period, users without 2FA configured are blocked from login until they set it up.
  5. SSO-authenticated users are exempt from this workspace-level 2FA requirement, since authentication is handled by the identity provider instead.

Title: Configuring SAML SSO with Okta
Summary:
To connect Okta as your SAML identity provider:

  1. In Okta, create a new SAML 2.0 app integration.
  2. Copy the Nimbus Workspace ACS URL and Entity ID (found under Workspace Settings > Security > Single Sign-On) into the Okta app configuration.
  3. In Okta, configure attribute statements to pass email and name to Nimbus Workspace.
  4. Download the Okta signing certificate and upload it into Nimbus Workspace's SSO configuration.
  5. Test with a non-Admin test user before enabling Enforce SSO workspace-wide, to avoid locking out Admins if a mapping is misconfigured.

Title: Configuring SAML SSO with Azure AD
Summary:
To connect Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) as your SAML identity provider:

  1. In Azure AD, create a new Enterprise Application using the non-gallery SAML option.
  2. Enter the Nimbus Workspace ACS URL and Entity ID from Workspace Settings > Security > Single Sign-On.
  3. Configure the SAML claims to map user.mail and user.displayname to the expected attributes.
  4. Download the Azure AD Federation Metadata XML and upload it into Nimbus Workspace.
  5. Assign the appropriate Azure AD user groups to the enterprise application, then test before enabling Enforce SSO.

Title: Configuring SAML SSO with Google Workspace
Summary:
To connect Google Workspace as your SAML identity provider:

  1. In the Google Admin console, add a new custom SAML app.
  2. Enter the Nimbus Workspace ACS URL and Entity ID from Workspace Settings > Security > Single Sign-On.
  3. Download the Google IdP metadata and upload it into Nimbus Workspace's SSO configuration.
  4. Map the standard email and name attributes in the Google Admin console's attribute mapping step.
  5. Turn on the SAML app for the appropriate organizational unit in Google Admin, then test a login before enabling Enforce SSO.

Title: Understanding Session Management Security
Summary: Nimbus Workspace issues a short-lived session token on login, refreshed silently in the background as long as you remain active, and fully expiring after the configured idle timeout (24 hours by default, adjustable by Enterprise Admins). Session tokens are bound to the originating device fingerprint, so a stolen token used from a substantially different device/browser combination triggers an additional verification challenge rather than being honored automatically.

Title: Locking an Account After Suspicious Activity
Summary: Admins can immediately lock a specific user's account (distinct from deactivation) if suspicious activity is suspected, blocking login instantly while preserving all account data and settings for investigation. Go to Team Directory, find the user, and select Lock Account from the action menu. A locked account can only be unlocked by an Admin after reviewing the Audit Log for that user's recent activity, or by Nimbus Workspace Support if the Admin's own account is the one in question.

Title: Reviewing the Security Audit Log
Summary: The Security Audit Log (Business/Enterprise) under Workspace Settings > Security > Audit Log records logins (including failures), password changes, role changes, SSO/2FA configuration changes, and data exports, each with a timestamp, actor, and source IP. Filter by user, event type, or date range, and export any filtered view to CSV for offline review or submission to an external security team during an investigation.

Title: Setting IP-Based Access Restrictions
Summary: See Restricting Login by IP Address for the full setup steps under Workspace Settings > Security > IP Allowlist. From a security-policy standpoint, this control is most effective combined with SSO enforcement, since it restricts both the network location and the identity provider through which access is possible, meaningfully narrowing the attack surface for account takeover attempts even if a password or session token were compromised.

Title: Understanding Data Encryption Standards
Summary: See Understanding Data Encryption at Rest and in Transit for full detail — in summary, AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, applied uniformly across all plan tiers, with keys managed through a dedicated key management service and rotated automatically on an annual schedule. Encryption standards are documented in full in the SOC 2 report available to Business and Enterprise customers under NDA.

Title: Reviewing Nimbus Workspace's Trust and Status Page
Summary: The Trust Center at trust.nimbusworkspace.com consolidates security documentation, current compliance certifications, the sub-processor list, and links to request the SOC 2 report or penetration test summary under NDA. It's separate from status.nimbusworkspace.com, which covers real-time system uptime and incident history rather than security/compliance posture — check the Trust Center first for any vendor security-review or procurement questionnaire.

Title: Understanding Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Summary: Access in Nimbus Workspace is enforced through role-based permissions at every layer — UI, API, and integrations all check the same underlying role/permission model, so a Guest-level API token cannot bypass restrictions the UI also enforces. Standard roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Guest) cover most needs; Business and Enterprise custom roles allow more granular permission combinations where the four standard roles don't fit an organization's structure precisely.

Title: Setting Up Approved Device Lists (Enterprise)
Summary:
Enterprise plans can restrict login to a list of approved device fingerprints (in addition to, not instead of, IP allowlisting) for organizations requiring managed-device-only access:

  1. Go to Workspace Settings > Security > Approved Devices.
  2. Enable Require Approved Devices.
  3. Have each user register their device on first login after enabling, which requires Admin approval.
  4. Review and approve pending device registrations from the same screen.
  5. Any login attempt from an unapproved device is blocked with an explanatory message, regardless of correct password and 2FA.

Title: Understanding Phishing Protection Measures
Summary: Nimbus Workspace enforces SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on all outbound system email to make spoofed "from Nimbus Workspace" phishing emails easier for receiving mail servers to reject automatically. All legitimate password reset and security emails link only to nimbusworkspace.com domains — Nimbus Workspace never asks for your password via email or embeds a login form directly inside an email. Report any suspicious email claiming to be from Nimbus Workspace to security@nimbusworkspace.com.

Title: Reporting a Phishing Email Impersonating Nimbus
Summary: If you receive a suspicious email impersonating Nimbus Workspace (asking you to "verify your account" via an unfamiliar link, for example), do not click any links or enter credentials. Forward the full email, including headers, to security@nimbusworkspace.com. Our security team investigates reported phishing campaigns and, where possible, works with hosting providers to have malicious lookalike domains taken down.

Title: Understanding Password Complexity Requirements
Summary: The platform-wide minimum password requirement is 8 characters including at least one number, applicable to all non-SSO accounts. Business and Enterprise Admins can strengthen this under Workspace Settings > Security > Password Policy, requiring up to 20 characters with mandatory uppercase, symbol, and periodic expiration rules (see Setting a Password Policy for Your Organization). SSO-enabled accounts have no Nimbus Workspace-side password at all, so this policy doesn't apply to them.

Title: Setting a Maximum Session Duration
Summary: Beyond the idle timeout (see Session Timeout Settings), Enterprise Admins can also set an absolute maximum session duration under Workspace Settings > Security > Session Policy — for example, forcing re-authentication every 8 hours regardless of activity level, which is stricter than an idle-only timeout and often required by regulated industries. This setting works alongside, not instead of, the idle timeout; whichever limit is reached first ends the session.

Title: Understanding Multi-Factor Authentication Options
Summary: Two 2FA methods are supported: a TOTP authenticator app (recommended, works offline, compatible with any standard authenticator like Google Authenticator or Authy) and SMS text message (simpler to set up but vulnerable to SIM-swapping attacks, and requires cellular signal). Enterprise Admins can restrict which method(s) are permitted workspace-wide under Workspace Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication, disabling SMS as an option if a stronger security posture is required.

Title: Reviewing Third-Party App Access
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Security > Connected Apps to see every OAuth application currently authorized to access your account, including the scopes each was granted and the date of authorization. Admins can view a workspace-wide equivalent under Workspace Settings > Security > Third-Party Access, covering every app any user in the workspace has authorized, which is useful for periodically auditing for apps that are no longer in active use.

Title: Revoking Access for a Connected App
Summary: To revoke a third-party app's access, go to Account Settings > Security > Connected Apps (or the workspace-wide equivalent for Admins reviewing another user's connections), find the app, and click Revoke Access. This immediately invalidates that app's OAuth token; if you want to reconnect the same app later, you'll need to go through its authorization flow again from scratch, since the original token cannot be reactivated once revoked.

Title: Understanding Data Loss Prevention Controls
Summary: See Configuring Data Loss Prevention Settings for setup steps. These Enterprise controls (restricting attachment types, disabling guest access workspace-wide, restricting bulk export to Admins) are preventive, additive restrictions layered on top of standard RBAC — they narrow what's possible beyond a user's role permissions, and cannot be used to grant additional access beyond what a role already allows.

Title: Setting Up Security Alerts for Admins
Summary: Beyond login notifications to individual users, Admins can configure proactive security alerts for workspace-wide events under Workspace Settings > Security > Admin Alerts — for example, a new Admin role assignment, a bulk data export, or an SSO/2FA configuration change. Alerts can be delivered by email or, if Slack/Teams is connected, posted directly to a designated security channel for faster visibility than email alone.

Title: Understanding SOC 2 Type II Compliance
Summary: SOC 2 Type II evaluates not just the design of security controls but their operating effectiveness over a sustained observation period (typically 6–12 months), audited by an independent third-party firm. Nimbus Workspace's report covers the Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust service criteria and is renewed annually. See Requesting a SOC 2 Report for how to obtain the current report under NDA.

Title: Understanding ISO 27001 Certification Status
Summary: Nimbus Workspace's current ISO 27001 certification status, along with the scope of certification and the certifying body, is published on the Trust Center at trust.nimbusworkspace.com and updated whenever certification is renewed or the scope changes. If ISO 27001 is a specific procurement requirement for your organization, confirm current status there rather than relying on historical documentation, since certification scope can evolve between renewal cycles.

Title: Reviewing the Responsible Disclosure Policy
Summary: The full Responsible Disclosure Policy at nimbusworkspace.com/security/disclosure outlines expected researcher conduct (no testing against other customers' data, no public disclosure before a fix is available), our commitment to acknowledge reports within 24 hours, and typical remediation timelines by severity. Researchers following this policy in good faith are given safe-harbor assurance against legal action for their testing activity, as detailed in the policy.

Title: Understanding Insider Threat Monitoring
Summary: Nimbus Workspace's internal access to customer data is logged and subject to least-privilege principles — employee access to production customer data requires a specific, time-boxed, and logged justification, reviewed periodically by our security team. This internal monitoring is distinct from the customer-facing Audit Log, which tracks activity within your own workspace by your own users, not Nimbus Workspace employee access to the underlying infrastructure.

Title: Setting Up Just-in-Time Provisioning with SSO
Summary: With SAML SSO configured, Enterprise workspaces can enable Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning so a new user is automatically created in Nimbus Workspace on their very first successful SSO login, without needing to be pre-invited manually. Enable this under Workspace Settings > Security > Single Sign-On > JIT Provisioning, and set a default role for JIT-created users. This is distinct from full SCIM provisioning, which also handles automatic deprovisioning; JIT alone only handles creation.

Title: Understanding Encryption Key Management
Summary: Encryption keys used for AES-256 at-rest encryption are managed through a dedicated cloud key management service, separate from the application layer that uses them, with automatic annual rotation and strict access logging on any key-management operation. Enterprise customers requiring customer-managed encryption keys (a "bring your own key" model) should discuss feasibility with their account executive, as this is evaluated as a custom Enterprise arrangement rather than a standard offering.

Title: Reviewing Login History for Your Account
Summary: Go to Account Settings > Security > Login History to see every login to your account over the past 90 days, including timestamp, approximate location, device type, and whether it was via password, SSO, or a linked Google/Microsoft account. This is a personal, read-only history distinct from the workspace-wide Security Audit Log available to Admins, and is a useful first check if you suspect unauthorized access.

Title: Understanding Account Lockout Thresholds
Summary: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window, an account is temporarily locked for 15 minutes as a brute-force protection measure, with an email notification sent describing the lockout. This threshold is fixed and not configurable on Team or Business plans; Enterprise Admins can adjust the failed-attempt threshold and lockout duration under Workspace Settings > Security > Account Lockout Policy.

Title: Setting Up Security Contact Notifications
Summary: Business and Enterprise workspaces can designate a security contact (a role-based email like security@yourcompany.com, distinct from any individual user account) to receive copies of security-relevant notifications — new Admin assignments, SSO configuration changes, bulk exports — under Workspace Settings > Security > Security Contact. This ensures continuity of security oversight even if the individual Admin who configured a setting later leaves the organization.

Title: Understanding Vulnerability Disclosure Timelines
Summary: Once a reported vulnerability is confirmed, Nimbus Workspace's internal target is to remediate critical-severity issues within 7 days, high-severity within 30 days, and medium/low-severity within 90 days, with the reporting researcher updated at each significant milestone. These are internal targets published for transparency in the Responsible Disclosure Policy, not contractual SLAs, though Enterprise customers with specific security-response SLA requirements can discuss custom terms through their account executive.

Title: Reviewing Nimbus Workspace's Penetration Testing Cadence
Summary: Nimbus Workspace commissions an independent third-party penetration test at least annually, covering the production application, API, and supporting infrastructure, in addition to continuous automated vulnerability scanning between formal tests. An executive summary of the most recent test is available to Business and Enterprise customers under NDA — see Requesting a Penetration Test Summary for how to obtain it.

Title: Understanding Fraud Detection on Payment Methods
Summary: Payment processing includes automated fraud screening (card verification, velocity checks on rapid repeated charge attempts, and geographic risk scoring) before a charge is authorized. A legitimate charge occasionally flagged as suspicious by this screening will show as declined even with correct card details — if you believe a decline was a false positive, contact your card issuer first, since the actual authorization decision is made by their fraud systems, not Nimbus Workspace's.

Title: Setting Organization-Wide IP Allowlists
Summary: See Restricting Login by IP Address and IP Allowlisting for API Access for the two related but separate controls — one restricts interactive login, the other restricts API token usage. Enterprise organizations typically configure both together for a consistent network-boundary security posture, ensuring that neither the web/mobile login path nor programmatic API access is reachable from outside approved network ranges.

Title: Understanding Device Trust and Remembered Devices
Summary: When you complete 2FA successfully, you can choose Remember This Device for 30 days, skipping the 2FA prompt on subsequent logins from that same specific browser/device combination while still requiring your password each time. This trust is scoped narrowly to one browser on one device — a different browser on the same computer, or the same browser after being cleared of cookies, will require 2FA again. Admins can disable the Remember This Device option workspace-wide for stricter environments.

Title: Reporting a Compromised Account
Summary:
If you believe your account has been compromised (unauthorized changes, logins you can't explain even after checking Login History), act immediately:

  1. Change your password right away from a device you trust.
  2. Go to Active Sessions and select Sign Out of All Devices.
  3. Enable or reset Two-Factor Authentication.
  4. Review the Security Audit Log (or ask an Admin to) for any unauthorized changes made during the compromise window.
  5. Email security@nimbusworkspace.com describing what you observed — our team can review server-side login and access logs beyond what's visible in your own Login History.
